es_SortDate: 2025-12-17T00:00:00.000+0000
beneficiaryAdministration: The objective of the call is to establish, develop, and/or improve cooperation between Lithuanian NGOs and advocacy-focused civil society organisations in other EU member states, strengthen organisational capacities, and promote collaboration in the field of advocacy, while upholding EU values. Expected impact includes new and strengthened cross-border partnerships, enhanced advocacy skills, increased mutual learning, and improved public understanding of EU values, including equality and the rights of persons belonging to minorities.
 Applications can e submitted in a single-stage procedure at any time starting on the date of call publication until January 31, 2027. All proposals first undergo administrative eligibility checks carried out by the Open Lithuania Foundation (OLF). Eligible applications are then assessed by two independent experts according to predefined quality criteria; if their scores differ by more than 30 points, a third expert is appointed. Following expert assessments, the two closest-scoring experts agree on a consolidated evaluation. The Selection Committee reviews the expert conclusions, may propose budgets adjustments, and approves the list of projects recommended for funding. Applications that fail to reach the minimum required scores or are not in compliance with EU values are excluded from further consideration.
 A total of 20 projects will be awarded grants of up to EUR 5,000 each within the maximum threshold allowed for financial support to third parties. Projects may last up to 6 months and will receive lump-sum funding paid in two instalments: 80% upon signing the grant agreement and 20% after the approval of final project reports. 
 Eligibility requirements for applicants: 
 The applicant is a legal entity registered in the Republic of Lithuania for at least one year prior to the announcement of the rolling call, i.e., no later than 16 December 2024.
 The applicant carries out activities in Lithuania.
 The applicant is an NGO established and operating in the Republic of Lithuania that meets the following definition “A non-profit voluntary organisation established as a legal entity, having a non-commercial purpose, independent of local, regional, and central government, public entities, political parties, and commercial organisations.” Religious institutions, trade unions, and political parties are not considered NGOs (definition in line with Article 2.3 of the Law on the Development of Non-Governmental Organizations).
 The applicant’s activities do not conflict with EU values and actively contribute (or seek to contribute) to the promotion of EU values.
 The applicant has submitted mandatory financial and annual activity reports to the National Center of Registers for the last two years (2023 and 2024), or financial and annual activity reports from the start of its activities if it has been operating for less than three years. Applicants applying after 1 June 2026 must have submitted mandatory financial and annual activity reports for 2024 and 2025.
 The Open Lithuania Foundation is not a shareholder of the applicant.
 NGOs already participating in the VERTA! Programme (Phase II, 2025–2027) are eligible only if the total cumulative budget of all their applications under the programme, including the amount requested in this call, does not exceed EUR 60,000.
 The applicant has not implemented any other bilateral cooperation project under the VERTA! Programme financed from the funds of this call.
 Eligibility requirements for partners: 
 The partner must be a non-governmental organization established and operating as a legal entity in one of the European Union Member States, excluding Lithuania;
 The partner conducts advocacy activities in the field of EU values and has at least two years of advocacy experience;
 Prior to submitting the application, the applicant and the partner have concluded and signed a letter of intent to cooperate or another type of partnership agreement defining the division of responsibilities.
 Further information, including a detailed description of the call procedure and the full eligibility criteria can be found here (in Lithuanian): Kvietimas dvišalio bendradarbiavimo projektams finansuoti - ALF

beneficiaryAdministration: Phortify Mobility Grants 
 Phortify Mobility Grants provide financial support to students and doctoral candidates participating in short-term mobility activities such as workshops, summer schools, conferences, and other events relevant to the thematic areas and objectives of the Phortify project.
 Supported activities are learning- and training-oriented, contribute to skills development in photonics and related digital technologies, and are implemented under the responsibility of Phortify partner institutions.
 Participating partners: 
 Ghent University (UGENT): 
 - Master of Science in Photonics Engineering (120 ECTS)
 Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e): 
 - Master of Science in Applied Physics (120 ECTS)
 - Master of Science in Electrical Engineering (120 ECTS): track (1) Semicon Devices and track (2) Connected World Technologies 
 Warsaw University of Technology (WUT): 
 - Master of Science in Mechatronics (90 ECTS)
 - Master of Science In Photonics (90 ECTS)
 Friedrich Schiller University (FSU): 
 - Master of Science in Photonics (120 ECTS)
 - Master of Science in Quantum Science & Technology (120 ECTS)
 How to apply for funding 
 Funding opportunities will be advertised through (1) the EU Funding & Tenders Portal, (2) the official Phortify website and (3) the official Phortify partner websites.
 Applications for Phortify funding must be submitted via the Phortify website. Applicants are required to consult the dedicated MyPhortify page , where all funding opportunities available under this pilot call are listed together with detailed application instructions and links to the relevant local application forms. 
 Nationality eligibility 
 Applicants must be nationals of an EU Member State, an associated country, or a country with which the European Union has an ongoing cooperation agreement under the Digital Europe Programme.
 Eligible countries include, inter alia, countries participating in Digital Partnerships, Trade and Technology Councils, digital dialogues, or other forms of ongoing international cooperation with the European Commission in the field of digital technologies.
 The authoritative list of eligible countries will be published as part of this call and may be updated in accordance with European Commission guidance.
 Eligibility 
 Under this call, Phortify Mobility Grants may be awarded to students belonging to one of the following categories:
 Bachelor and Master students
 PhD students enrolled at a Phortify university, provided that the mobility activity is directly linked to their academic training and teaching activities
 In all cases, eligible applicants must be students at the time of the mobility and the mobility must:
 be directly related to the thematic areas and objectives of the Phortify project
 contribute to the academic and professional development of the student
 be carried out during the student’s period of study
 be implemented under the responsibility of a Phortify partner institution
 General university staff members who are not enrolled as students or doctoral candidates are not eligible under this call. 
 Applicants must submit the following documentation:
 Latest official academic BSc and MSc (if applicable) transcripts 
 A Phortify-specific motivation letter , describing the applicant’s motivation for applying for Phortify funding and their alignment with the objectives of the Phortify project
 A curriculum vitae (CV)
 Applications that fail to meet the minimum eligibility requirements or that do not include the required documentation will be declared ineligible and will not be further evaluated.
 Evaluation and selection 
 The predefined evaluation framework applicable to this call is published on the Phortify website as a dedicated evaluation framework document and is applied by all partners for all applications under this call.
 1. Purpose and Scope 
 This description defines the evaluation framework applied to applications submitted under the Phortify Mobility Grants – Pilot Call.
 The framework ensures transparency, equal treatment of applicants, consistency across partner institutions, and alignment with the objectives of the Phortify project, including its Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) principles.
 2. Evaluation Principles 
 The evaluation process is based on the following principles:
 Transparency and traceability of decisions
 Equal and fair treatment of all applicants
 Merit-based selection
 Consideration of DEI objectives in line with EU guidance
 3. Evaluation Process Overview 
 The evaluation consists of two sequential stages:
 Eligibility verification (pass/fail)
 Comparative assessment and ranking
 4. Stage 1 – Eligibility Verification 
 Applications are checked for compliance with all eligibility requirements defined in the call text. Applicants must submit all required supporting documentation, including academic transcripts, a Phortify-specific motivation letter, and a curriculum vitae (CV).
 Applications that fail to meet the eligibility requirements or that do not include the required documentation are declared ineligible and are not further evaluated.
 5. Stage 2 – Comparative Assessment 
 Eligible applications are assessed comparatively using the criteria below. Each criterion is scored independently on a scale from 0 to 5 points.
 Evaluation Criteria 
 Academic Excellence (0/5): Academic performance, relevance of previous studies, and preparedness for the proposed mobility.
 Motivation and Alignment with Phortify Objectives (0/5): Quality, coherence, and relevance of the motivation letter, including alignment with Phortify’s educational and societal objectives.
 Overall Applicant Profile (0/5): Skills, experience, background, and potential contribution to the Phortify community, as reflected in the CV.
 Maximum total score: 15 points.
 Ranking and Allocation of Funding 
 Funding under this call is awarded following a rolling call procedure. Applications may be submitted at any time while the call is open. Applications are evaluated at regular intervals, typically every 2 to 3 months , or earlier if the number of submitted applications or budget availability so requires.
 Following each evaluation round, eligible applications are ranked in order of merit, and funding is allocated until the available budget under this call is exhausted. In cases of oversubscription , priority is given to higher-ranked applications. Where applications receive identical or comparable evaluation results, tie-break rules promoting underrepresented groups, including women and students from disadvantaged socio-economic backgrounds, will be applied in line with Phortify DEI objectives.
 Selection Committees 
 Applications are evaluated by local selection committees established by the Phortify partner institutions. Committees apply this evaluation framework consistently and impartially. Members must declare any conflicts of interest and ensure appropriate mitigation measures.
 Documentation and transparency 
 Evaluation outcomes and funding decisions are documented by the partner institutions. Awarded grants are communicated to the Phortify Coordinator. Aggregate data will be reported in accordance with the project’s reporting obligations.
 Available funding under this call 
 Type and duration of financial support 
 Financial support under this call is provided in the form of lump-sum grants. Lump-sum amounts not linked to duration are established on the basis of estimated actual costs and are intended to contribute to expenses related to participation in the supported mobility activity, such as travel, accommodation, subsistence, and, where applicable, registration or participation fees.
 UGENT: 
 - Phortify Mobility Grants for joining a selected event, workshop or summer school of € 1.000 - lump sum not linked to duration 
 TU/e: 
 - Phortify Mobility Grants for joining a selected international event, workshop or summer school of € 2.000 - lump sum not linked to duration 
 - Phortify Mobility Grants for joining a selected national or international event of € 500 - lump sum not linked to duration 
 WUT: 
 - Phortify Mobility Grants for joining a selected event, workshop or summer school of € 2.000 - lump sum not linked to duration 
 FSU: 
 - Phortify Mobility Grant for participation in the Jena Quantum Hackathon or the DokDok conference 2026 of € 800 - lump sum not linked to duration 
 Financial support may only be used for the activities listed above; no other activities are eligible.
description: About Phortify 
 Phortify - Photonics Education Network for Next-Gen Innovation and Digital Skills Excellence for Industry and Society - is dedicated to the Enhancement and Harmonisation of Photonics education and training across Europe. Phortify offers a two-year European Master’s in Photonics Engineering, combining advanced coursework, hands-on laboratory training, and cutting-edge digital skills development, structured mobility windows and industry placements. Students who complete the Phortify track receive an official Phortify Certificate in addition to their Master’s degree. Students can enrol in a Phortify-related master programme at any of the 7 participating universities. In addition, Phortify provides stand-alone modules with harmonised standards for quality assurance and certification, offering high flexibility and mobility for both students and industry professionals. Finally, Phortify organises mentoring programmes for women postdocs and early PIs as well as one-day immersive experience events for prospective students, providing a unique opportunity to explore photonics and its applications.
 About the Phortify Funding Framework 
 Phortify’s Funding Framework aims to widen participation in photonics by supporting students and staff who are traditionally underrepresented in STEM. This includes women and gender minorities, students from low-income or socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds, first-generation university students, and learners with disabilities or specific support needs. The programme also encourages participation from regions with limited access to advanced higher education, as well as those belonging to cultural or minority groups that may be underrepresented in higher education. By addressing these dimensions of diversity, Phortify helps ensure a more inclusive and equitable community of future photonics professionals. Participants selected for Phortify funding receive financial support for studies and mobility pathways within the participating master programmes, or for mentoring programmes and STEM experience workshops organised by one of the Phortify partners.

This includes women and gender minorities, students from low-income or socio-economically disadvantaged backgrounds, first-generation university students, and learners with disabilities or specific support needs. The programme also encourages participation from regions with limited access to advanced higher education, as well as those belonging to cultural or minority groups that may be underrepresented in higher education. By addressing these dimensions of diversity, Phortify helps ensure a more inclusive and equitable community of future photonics professionals. Participants selected for Phortify funding receive financial support for studies and mobility pathways within the participating master programmes, or for mentoring programmes and STEM experience workshops organised by one of the Phortify partners.

furtherInformation: INTERNSHIP OPPORTUNITY 
 TITLE OF INTERNSHIP: Hands-On AI & Data Science Internships
 LOCATION:  
 Remote (Virtual) or On-Site at Informatics Institute of Middle East Technical University
 DURATION: 4 weeks
 ELIGIBLE CANDIDATES: Biology, Molecular Biology and Genetics, Engineering, and Biomedical - Bioinformatics Students (BSc/MSc)
 OVERVIEW 
 The Informatics Institute provides a unique research and learning environment across the interdisciplinary fields of medical informatics, bioinformatics, data informatics, and information systems. 
 We're offering exciting internship opportunities for students passionate about Artificial Intelligence (AI), Data Science, and Digital Health Technologies. This hands-on experience will deeply immerse you in: 
 Nextflow Pipelines: You'll work with NextFlow computational workflows, seamlessly integrated with container technologies like Docker and Singularity, for critical analyses such as differential gene expression and differential ChIP-seq. 
 SigProfiler Suite: You'll gain expertise with the powerful SigProfiler tools specialized in cancer genomics, including SigProfilerMatrixGenerator, SigProfilerSimulator, SigProfilerExtractor, SigProfilerAssignment, and SigProfilerTopography. 
 This experience will transform your theoretical knowledge into practical, in-demand skills, preparing you for a successful career in data-driven scientific fields. 
 DELIVERY MODE & WORK ENVIRONMENT 
 Virtual Internships: A cost-effective alternative allowing students to work remotely. 
 On-Site Internships: Available in the classroom at the Informatics Institute for students who prefer in-person collaboration. 
 Hybrid Approach: Combining remote and on-site work for flexibility. 
 Interns will work in small interdisciplinary teams under the guidance of mentors, engaging in collaborative research and development. 
 WHAT YOU WILL WORK ON 
 Building Robust Nextflow Pipelines: Developing and optimizing Nextflow computational workflows that leverage Docker and Singularity container technologies. These pipelines will be crucial for performing advanced analyses like differential gene expression and differential ChIP-seq. 
 Mastering the SigProfiler Suite: Becoming proficient with a suite of powerful SigProfiler tools, specifically SigProfilerMatrixGenerator, SigProfilerSimulator, SigProfilerExtractor, SigProfilerAssignment, and SigProfilerTopography. 
 TECHNOLOGIES YOU’LL USE  
 Python, R 
 Nextflow 
 SigProfiler suite of tools 
 WHAT WE EXPECT FROM YOU 
 Curiosity and willingness to learn 
 Python programming knowledge 
 Interest in computational biology and bioinformatics 
 Teamwork skills 
 LEARNING OUTCOMES 
 Upon completion, interns will: 
 ✅ Design & Implement Nextflow Pipelines. 
 ✅ Master Containerization Technologies. 
 ✅ Ensure Workflow Reproducibility. 
 ✅ Manage Large-Scale Data. 
 ✅ Mastering the powerful SigProfiler tools for cancer genomics analysis. 
 ASSESSMENT & CERTIFICATION 
 Completion of assigned tasks and active participation in projects. 
 Development of a mini research report or technical presentation at the end of the internship. 
 Issuance of an Internship Certificate by the Informatics Institute of Middle East Technical University. 
 APPLICATION PROCESS 
 Interested students should submit: 
 📌 A short CV highlighting relevant skills and background. 
 📌 A brief motivation letter (max. 1 page) explaining their interest in the internship. 
 📩 Applications should be sent to: [burcako@metu.edu.tr] with the subject: 
 “SUSA Internship Application – [Your Name]” 
 For more details, visit contact [burcako@metu.edu.tr]. 
 This internship offers a unique opportunity to fill the gap between foundational academic knowledge and the practical, industry-ready skills required to excel in the rapidly evolving landscape of data-driven digital health. 
 Financial support will be available to facilitate student mobility. SUSA students will have access to internship opportunities offered by both consortium members and affiliated ecosystem partners. The selection criteria for these internships will be developed collaboratively through a co-design process and will incorporate Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) principles, with particular attention to gender and the socio-economic background of applicants.
 Student exchanges between Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) will be further supported through a structured and mentored Erasmus+ mobility initiative. To assist students in planning their mobility paths, joint SUSA learning activities will be organized. Additionally, the SUSA Virtual Academy will host a dedicated matchmaking platform, enabling students and teachers to explore internship opportunities and allowing healthcare ecosystem stakeholders to promote openings and connect with emerging talent.

 OVERVIEW 
 Gnomon Informatics SA, a leading informatics company specializing in digital health solutions, is offering internship opportunities for students interested in Artificial Intelligence (AI), Data Science, and Digital Health Technologies. This internship provides hands-on experience with eHealthPass , a certified patient-centered platform for remote patient monitoring, which includes a mobile app for patients and a web application for healthcare professionals . eHealthPass is a solution for remote care, virtual care and hospital at home, as well as communication and patient empowerment tool, putting patient in the middle and allowing patient to become stakeholder in own care instead of being mere subject of care. Behind eHealthPass there is also the eHealthPass.CDR , a platform providing and enabling HIE (Health Information Exchange) – complete lifecycle management of structured and unstructured clinical documents and clinical data, and their secure sharing/exchange. 
 Interns will contribute to AI development, data quality enhancement , and predictive analytics in healthcare , gaining invaluable experience in a multidisciplinary setting . 
 INTERNSHIP TRACKS 
 1. Medical Students – AI and Digital Health Applications 
 Assisting in training AI models by feeding them with structured and unstructured medical data. 
 Understanding and improving AI-assisted decision support tools for clinical applications. 
 Exploring ways to generate customized outcomes and predictions for individual patients. 
 Medical file structures and content (questionnaires, educational and other materials) 
 Usability of the product 
 2. Engineering & Data Science Students – Data & AI Optimization 
 Contributing to data quality assessment and enhancing data mesh architecture . 
 Developing and testing AI tools for predictive analytics and patient monitoring. 
 Exploring interoperability challenges in digital health using HL7 FHIR and other HL7 standards (HL7v2 messages, HL7 CDA) . 
 Assisting in data visualization techniques to support decision-making for healthcare providers (UX/UI for HealthTech)

 Terminology management

 R&D Projects: Contribute to European Research Projects and pilot implementations in real healthcare settings. 
 TECHNOLOGIES YOU’LL USE 
 Java/ Spring Boot/ Python 
 FHIR/ HL7/ IHE 
 Azure/ AWS/ Docker/ Kubernetes 
 AI Models/ Prompt Engineering/ LLMs 
 WHAT WE EXPECT FROM YOU 
 Curiosity and willingness to learn 
 Basic programming knowledge (preferably Jana or Python) 
 Interest in healthcare or AI 
 Teamwork skills 
 LEARNING OUTCOMES 
 Upon completion, interns will: 
 ✅ Gain practical experience in digital health platforms and AI integration. 
 ✅ Understand data governance, privacy regulations (GDPR), and interoperability . 
 ✅ Develop hands-on skills in data science, machine learning, and healthcare informatics .

 Applications are open from April 28, 2026. The deadline to submit the applications is June 28, 2026, at 4.00 p.m. (Eastern European Time, EET). 
 Applicants are required to complete the Application Form and upload the following documents, clearly labelled with the applicant's name: 
 1) Signed Application Letter (Annex 1);
 2) Curriculum Vitae;
 3) Short Motivation Letter;
 4) Supporting Documents for each claimed eligibility criterion, issued by a responsible authority or accredited expert.
 Applications must be submitted in English. Supporting documents may be submitted in English. If the provided documentation is insufficient, the Evaluation Committee may request additional information or reject the application.
 Evaluation Committee
 A Joint Evaluation Committee, appointed by TU Wien, will review all applications. The Committee will include:
 ● Representatives of TU Wien (4 persons) 
 ● At least one student representative of TU Wien ;
 ● At least one representative from the EURIDICE consortium partners.
 The Committee will finalize the evaluation by June 30.
 The Joint Evaluation Committee will assess each application and assign points according to the following criteria:
 1. Academic and Social Achievements 
 - Academic performance, scientific, volunteering, and social activities: 5- 20 points. 
 2. Certified Disabilities 
 - Based on verified disability documentation: 5 points. 
 3. Low Socio-Economic Background 
 - Applicants whose family income falls between the first quartile (Q1) and the median income (Q2) in their country of origin will receive will receive 5 points. The reference fiscal year is the year preceding the application. 
 All applications will be ranked based on the total number of points obtained across the four criteria. Each application may receive a maximum of 30 points in total. A total of 5 scholarships will be awarded. 
 The decision of the Evaluation Committee is final. 
 The list of selected scholarship recipients will be published on the EURIDICE website at TU Wien. 
 Purpose, Amount, and Duration of the Scholarship
 TU Wien hereby announces a Call for Applications for the Digital Humanism Summer School 2026, this call is issued within the framework of the activities planned under the Project European Inclusive Education for Digital Society, Social Innovation and Global Citizenship (EURIDICE), and is intended for masters students and young researchers across different fields of study of specialized modules as produced under the EURIDICE project in the 2025/2026 academic year. The total budget allocated for this Call amounts to EUR 13.140,00.
 The Scholarship Programme is designed to provide financial support to students participating in the Digital Humanism Summer School. Its objectives are to:
 ● support students from underprivileged or vulnerable backgrounds by providing them with equal access to international learning opportunities;
 ● promote inclusiveness, diversity, fairness, and gender balance in higher education;
 ● cover participation fee, accommodation and travel costs.
 The scholarship also serves as a form of social support, helping students overcome personal or socio-economic barriers that hinder participation in international education.
 The scholarship is awarded as a lump sum for a one-week period. There is no automatic entitlement or renewal.
 The amount of the scholarship is EUR 1100.00 per external student (this lump sum covers participation fee, accommodation for six nights, and travel expenses to and from Vienna), or EUR 480 for students residing in Vienna. 
 Expected duration ofthe Scholarship Programme: 1 week.
 Scholarships will be awarded based on the evaluation scores (see Article 5 – Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure). A maximum of 30 points can be awarded per application.
 Eligibility Criteria
 1. Eligible applicants include all students from European countries and countries associated to DIGITAL EUROPE PROGRAMME who face financial challenges during their studies.
 2. Students are also encouraged to apply if they meet one or more of the following criteria:
 1. Students with Certified Disabilities 
 Students with certified disabilities may apply for a Summer School scholarship. According to Article 1 of the European Disability Policy, persons with disabilities are defined as those who have long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments which in interaction with various barriers may hinder their full and effective participation in society on an equal basis with others. Applicants must provide certified medical documentation or proof of national disability status. 
 2. Students with Low Socio-Economic Backgrounds 
 Students from families with low socio-economic conditions are eligible to apply. Low socio- economic status is defined according to students' family income. Required proofs include a tax statement, income certificate, or official social benefit statement. 
 This call (as well as the financial support that will be provided through it) is NOT an EU action. This call is launched solely by the TU Wien. 
 The financial support to the selected successful applicants will be provided directly by TU Wien in its own name and under its own responsibility. The publication of this call in the EU Funding & Tenders Portal is made solely for information purposes with the aim to increase the visibility of this call to the general public, including to potential applicants (i.e. students). The said publication shall not be construed as direct or indirect approval of the content and conditions of this call by the relevant EU authorities or as any form of waiver from the above-described responsibility of TU Wien.

 2) Curriculum Vitae;
 3) Short Motivation Letter;
 4) Supporting Documents for each claimed eligibility criterion, issued by a responsible authority or accredited expert.
 Applications must be submitted in English. Supporting documents may be submitted in English. If the provided documentation is insufficient, the Evaluation Committee may request additional information or reject the application.
 Evaluation Committee
 A Joint Evaluation Committee, appointed by TU Wien, will review all applications. The Committee will include:
 ● Representatives of TU Wien (4 persons) 
 ● At least one student representative of TU Wien ;
 ● At least one representative from the EURIDICE consortium partners.
 The Committee will finalize the evaluation by June 30.
 The Joint Evaluation Committee will assess each application and assign points according to the following criteria:
 1. Academic and Social Achievements 
 - Academic performance, scientific, volunteering, and social activities: 5- 20 points. 
 2. Certified Disabilities 
 - Based on verified disability documentation: 5 points. 
 3. Low Socio-Economic Background 
 - Applicants whose family income falls between the first quartile (Q1) and the median income (Q2) in their country of origin will receive will receive 5 points. The reference fiscal year is the year preceding the application. 
 All applications will be ranked based on the total number of points obtained across the four criteria. Each application may receive a maximum of 30 points in total. A total of 5 scholarships will be awarded. 
 The decision of the Evaluation Committee is final. 
 The list of selected scholarship recipients will be published on the EURIDICE website at TU Wien. 
 Purpose, Amount, and Duration of the Scholarship
 TU Wien hereby announces a Call for Applications for the Digital Humanism Summer School 2026, this call is issued within the framework of the activities planned under the Project European Inclusive Education for Digital Society, Social Innovation and Global Citizenship (EURIDICE), and is intended for masters students and young researchers across different fields of study of specialized modules as produced under the EURIDICE project in the 2025/2026 academic year. The total budget allocated for this Call amounts to EUR 13.140,00.
 The Scholarship Programme is designed to provide financial support to students participating in the Digital Humanism Summer School. Its objectives are to:
 ● support students from underprivileged or vulnerable backgrounds by providing them with equal access to international learning opportunities;
 ● promote inclusiveness, diversity, fairness, and gender balance in higher education;
 ● cover participation fee, accommodation and travel costs.
 The scholarship also serves as a form of social support, helping students overcome personal or socio-economic barriers that hinder participation in international education.
 The scholarship is awarded as a lump sum for a one-week period. There is no automatic entitlement or renewal.
 The amount of the scholarship is EUR 1100.00 per external student (this lump sum covers participation fee, accommodation for six nights, and travel expenses to and from Vienna), or EUR 480 for students residing in Vienna. 
 Expected duration ofthe Scholarship Programme: 1 week.
 Scholarships will be awarded based on the evaluation scores (see Article 5 – Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure). A maximum of 30 points can be awarded per application.
 Eligibility Criteria
 1. Eligible applicants include all students from European countries and countries associated to DIGITAL EUROPE PROGRAMME who face financial challenges during their studies.
 2. Students are also encouraged to apply if they meet one or more of the following criteria:
 1. Students with Certified Disabilities 
 Students with certified disabilities may apply for a Summer School scholarship. According to Article 1 of the European Disability Policy, persons with disabilities are defined as those who have long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments which in interaction with various barriers may hinder their full and effective participation in society on an equal basis with others. Applicants must provide certified medical documentation or proof of national disability status. 
 2. Students with Low Socio-Economic Backgrounds 
 Students from families with low socio-economic conditions are eligible to apply. Low socio- economic status is defined according to students' family income. Required proofs include a tax statement, income certificate, or official social benefit statement. 
 This call (as well as the financial support that will be provided through it) is NOT an EU action. This call is launched solely by the TU Wien. 
 The financial support to the selected successful applicants will be provided directly by TU Wien in its own name and under its own responsibility. texto:
es_SortDate: 2026-09-21T00:00:00.000+0000
beneficiaryAdministration: The AI4GreenDeal project delivers a 120-ECTS Master’s double-degree programme combining energy-domain knowledge with data and AI skills and with innovation and entrepreneurship training, complemented by flexible, stackable self-standing modules. Through this call, the consortium offers to students (Financial Support to Third Parties (FSTP)) in the form of full or partial scholarships to attract highly qualified candidates and to widen access to the programme, in line with the project’s target of at least 30% participation from women and/or individuals from lower socio-economic backgrounds.
 Two scholarship schemes are offered under this call:
 Energy Impact Scholarships — awarded to applicants who demonstrate strong academic preparation and potential to contribute to the energy transition.
 Diversity, Entrepreneurship and Digital Champions (DED) Scholarships — awarded across three strands (DEI; Entrepreneurship; Digital Champions) to promote diversity and recognise entrepreneurial or digital-innovation excellence.
 Applications are submitted through the InnoEnergy Masters+ online application tool within the published application window: 
 https://apply.innoenergy.com/courses/course/55-masters-advanced-energy-systems-and-ai .
 The MSc in Advanced Energy Systems and AI operates a rolling intake with five application rounds between 21 September 2026 and 30 May 2027; scholarship decisions are taken after each round within the overall framework and budget communicated for the intake.

 No separate scholarship application is required: every applicant admitted to the programme is automatically considered for an Energy Impact Scholarship and admitted applicants who submit a 1–2 minute motivation video and pay the registration fee may in addition be considered for a DED Scholarship.
 Each application is assessed in three stages. The Admissions Office first verifies document validity, general admissibility, recipient eligibility, and exclusion criteria. The Programme Steering Committee — composed of academic representatives of the partner universities acting as independent experts — then confirms programme-specific eligibility, evaluates, and ranks eligible applicants against the published award criteria.( https://ai4greendeal.com/content/uploads/2026/09/AI4GreenDeal_Indicative_Evaluation_Rubrics_070926.pdf ) The programme-independent DED Selection Committee additionally evaluates DED applicants. 
 Before scoring, every evaluator signs a declaration of confidentiality and absence of conflict of interest. Committee decisions require a quorum, and each round is closed with a signed selection-confirmation report. Scholarship awards are approved by the FSTP Management Office and communicated by official acceptance letter issued by the Admissions Office and signed by the Programme Director. Applicants must confirm participation within five working days of the acceptance letter.
 Applicants may appeal decisions on general admissibility or programme-specific eligibility within the period stated in the rejection communication. Scholarship and ranking outcomes are not subject to academic appeal but may be reviewed for procedural compliance.
 In case students decline their offer for a scholarship or scholarship funding cannot be allocated because of applicants not fulfilling the minimum thresholds, the remaining budget will move to the next available cut-off moment. If after the fifth cut-off moment, budget is remaining, it may be allocated to students from previous rounds in the order of scoring (highest to lowest). 
 Eligible countries 
 Scholarship recipients must be natural persons holding the nationality of one of the DEP eligible countries, which for the intake 2027 is the list of countries below Should the list of DEP eligible countries change, then other nationalities may become eligible. 
 EU Member States and Associated Digital Europe Programme (DEP) Countries : Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Iceland, Norway, Liechtenstein, Switzerland.
 Other Eligible Non-EU Countries: Albania, Algeria, Armenia, Argentina, Australia, Azerbaijan, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Brazil, Canada, Egypt, Georgia, India, Israel, Japan, Jordan, Kosovo, Lebanon, Libya, Mexico, Moldova, Montenegro, Morocco, North Macedonia, Palestine, Serbia, Singapore, South Korea, Syria, Taiwan, Tunisia, Ukraine, United States.
 Common eligibility and exclusion grounds 
 The conditions in this section apply to both the Energy Impact Scholarships and the DED Scholarships. Scheme-specific eligibility conditions are set out under each scholarship.
 Common eligibility conditions 
 To be eligible for a scholarship under this call, an applicant must:
 hold the nationality of one of the countries listed in eligible countries.
 be admitted to the MSc in Advanced Energy Systems and AI; and
 accept the InnoEnergy Student Code of Conduct.
 Exclusion grounds 
 An applicant is excluded from consideration for any scholarship under this call, and any scholarship already awarded may be withdrawn, where the applicant:
 has previously received an InnoEnergy scholarship.
 has submitted false or materially misleading information at any point in the application process.
 is receiving other EU funding covering the same participation costs (no double funding); or
 is subject to EU restrictive measures.
 The Admissions Office verifies these conditions on the basis of documentary evidence and records the outcome in the application tool. Applicants who do not meet the common eligibility conditions or who fall under an exclusion ground are excluded from scholarship support, with the reason recorded.
 1. Energy Impact Scholarships 
 The Energy Impact Scholarships are awarded to applicants who demonstrate strong academic preparation and potential to contribute to the energy transition. Both full and partial scholarships are available. Selection is intrinsically linked to admission: every applicant admitted to the MSc is automatically considered, and no separate scholarship application is required.
 Who is considered? 
 An application is admissible where the applicant has:
 submitted the complete online application within the published deadline and in the required certified format.
 obtained (or will obtain before enrolment) a Bachelor’s degree of at least 180 ECTS, or an equivalent academic qualification from an internationally recognised university, or qualifies for conditional admission; and
 demonstrated English-language proficiency through an accepted test (IELTS Academic overall ≥ 6.5 with no section below 5.5; TOEFL iBT ≥ 92 with writing ≥ 22; or Cambridge CAE/CPE grades A–C), or through a documented exemption. Where the Year-2 host university requires it, a valid test result must be submitted by 15 July (intermediate) and 30 July (final) before the academic year starts.
 The Admissions Office verifies admissibility. Late or incomplete applications are not admissible and are not grounds for appeal.
 Programme-specific eligibility. 
 In addition to the common eligibility conditions, applicants for an Energy Impact Scholarship must hold a completed Bachelor’s degree of 180 ECTS or equivalent in engineering (mechanical, electronic, electrical, civil) or a related science, with prior coverage of the fundamentals of electrical and mechanical engineering. The Programme Steering Committee confirms programme-specific eligibility.

 2. Diversity, Entrepreneurship and Digital Champions (DED) Scholarships 
 The DED Scholarships promote diversity and inclusion and recognise entrepreneurial achievement or excellence in digital innovation for energy and sustainability. The scheme comprises three strands — Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI); Entrepreneurship; and Digital Champions — and is evaluated by the programme-independent DED Selection Committee, composed of representatives of InnoEnergy and the partner universities, and not linked to any specific MSc programme. Full and partial scholarships are available.
 Who is considered? 
 An application to the DED scheme is admissible only where the applicant has:

 submitted a motivation video of 1 to 2 minutes indicating one DED strand, uploaded through the InnoEnergy Masters+ online application tool. Videos exceeding the two-minute limit are excluded. 
 The Admissions Office transmits the list of admissible and eligible applicants to the DED Selection Committee after the registration-fee deadline for each round.
 Strand-specific eligibility 
 In addition to the common eligibility conditions, applicants for a DED Scholarship must meet the strand-specific profile requirements: relevant D&I engagement, gender-balance contribution, entrepreneurial experience, or digital-innovation project experience, as applicable to the selected strand.

 Scholarship coverage and associated rights 
 What follows in this section — on scholarship coverage, associated rights, and the items covered and not covered — applies equally to the Energy Impact Scholarships and the DED Scholarships. The scholarship — whether full or partial — is expressed as a waiver of the participation fee for the MSc in Advanced Energy Systems and AI. The sections below set out what the scholarship covers, what remains for the recipient’s own account, and how the scholarship value relates to the amount declared as Financial Support to Third Parties.
 Items covered by the scholarship 
 The full and partial scholarships are intended to cover, in whole or in part, the costs associated with the following items:
 Institutional enrolment at the host universities, including access to courses, exercises, and laboratory sessions (where applicable).

 Administrative services.

 Travel to and from the host universities.

beneficiaryAdministration: The CoPower Action has been designed to directly fund initiatives addressing Gender Based Violence(GBV) against women, girls and children through an intersectional approach .
 All eligible activities supported through the project calls will directly respond to the multidimensional and intersecting needs of women, girls, and child survivors of GBV, strengthening an inclusive and accessible protection systems across different intervention contexts. Child protection and gender mainstreaming are expected to be integral components of the proposals submitted by CSOs, while partner organisations will provide dedicated technical support to improve the capacities of participating CSOs in these areas. 
 3 NATIONAL CALLS 
 Three national calls will support CSOs in Italy, Greece and Spain focusing on: Comprehensive and inclusive support for women and girls' victims of GBV . 
 TARGET APPLICANTS 
 The calls target small and medium-sized grassroots CSOs , particularly those operating in rural, peripherical or marginalised areas and legally registered in Italy, Greece or Spain. The primary target group, will include Women’s rights organisations (WROs), Anti-violence centres and anti-trafficking centres, Human rights, LGBTIQ+ rights, child rights, social inclusion and disability, elderly, migrant and refugee organisations. 
 2 FUNDING WORKSTREAMS: 
 1. Enhanced protection response for women, girls and children, victims of GBV, adopting an intersectional approach. This area focusses on providing tailored protection and support services, including safe houses, medical and psychological assistance for women and girls, in all their diversity, who are victims of domestic, sexual violence and other forms of GBV considering specific barriers for equal access to protection (Budget: 540,000 EUR in total for the 3 Countries). 
 2. Reduction of harmful practices , with a focus on improving interventions against harmful practices such as female genital mutilation, intersex genital mutilation, forced abortion, forced sterilisation, child and forced marriage, and honour-related violence, forced medicalisation of transgender women. Funded projects will aim at both 9 preventing and responding to these practices, with a particular focus on raising awareness, strengthening legal frameworks, and providing education to communities at risk (Budget: 360,000 EUR in total for the 3 Countries). 
 CALL TIMELINE 
 First Round : 
 Opening: 24/08/2026 ( 11/09/2026 in Greece) 
 Deadline: 23/11/2026 at 15.00 CET 
 Second Round : 
 Opening: 01/12/2026 
 Deadline: 01/03/2027 at 15.00 CET 
 AVAILABLE GRANT PER COUNTRY : 
 First Round - 6 projects of the following amounts will be awarded: 
 Stream 1: one grant of EUR 50,000; one grant of EUR 50,000; one grant of EUR 20,000 
 Stream 2: one grant of EUR 50,000; one grant of EUR 25,000; one grant of EUR 5,000 
 Second Round - 4 projects of the following amounts will be awarded: 
 Stream 1: one grant of EUR 30,000; one grant of EUR 30,000; 
 Stream 2: one grant of EUR 20,000; one grant of EUR 20,000 
 APPLICATION PROCESS: 
 Administrative check 
 Eligibility requirements verification and shortlisting 
 Final assessment and selection 
 Pre-notification and Due diligence 
 Confirmation and signing the agreement 
 Information session are foreseen online and in present in each country. 
 For more information please visit: https://copower.oxfam.it/ 
 Contact: infocopower@oxfam.it

furtherInformation: The CoPower project is implemented by Oxfam Italia ETS, Action Aid Hellas, Asociación Bienestar y Desarolloa and We World-GVC. It started on 1 March 2026 and will end on 28 February 2029.
 Its objective is to strengthen the capacity of Civil Society Organisation (CSOs) to provide safe and inclusive services for victims of gender-based violence (GBV) against women, girls, and children in all their diversity across six European countries: Italy, Greece, Spain, Serbia, Romania, and Albania.
 The project foresees three national calls, along with transnational calls involving the following country pairs: Italy–Serbia, Spain-Romania, and Greece-Albania. The national calls will fund at least 10 projects in Italy, 10 in Spain and 10 in Greece. The transnational calls will fund 5 projects for Italy and Serbia, 5 projects for Spain and Romania and 5 projects for Greece and Albania. Overall, a minimum of 60 CSOs will be engaged, fostering meaningful cross-country cooperation.
 A comprehensive capacity-sharing programme for CSOs will include needs assessments, training, mentoring, and both national and international workshops to promote mutual learning and support in the full implementation of the EU Violence Against Women Directive.

titulo: Specialised education programmes or modules in key capacity areas
texto:
es_SortDate: 2026-07-08T00:00:00.000+0000
beneficiaryAdministration: 1.Summary and purpose of the call 
 The Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya – Barcelona TECH (hereinafter “UPC”) is soliciting applications for scholarships grants (hereinafter “scholarships”) to support students of the master's degree program “Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries” (hereinafter “AI4CI Master”) taught at UPC Castelldefels School of Telecommunications and Aerospace Engineering (hereinafter “EETAC”) in Castelldefels, Spain
 The UPC- AI4CI scholarships is granted by the “Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries” (hereinafter “AI4CI project”). The AI4CI project is co-funded by the European Union within the under the Grant Agreement No. 101123524 funded under the topic DIGITAL-2022-SKILLS-03-SPECIALISED-EDU - Specialised education programmes or modules in key capacity areas.
 The maximum funding available under this call is €167,500 and may be awarded until the available budget is fully exhausted, provided that this occurs within the overall implementation period of the AI4CI project.
 The indicative total number of scholarships to be awarded is approximately 49 ranging from 500 EUR to 4,500 EUR.
 The aim of the scholarships is that recipients benefit from AI4CI project's high-quality education in digital areas and to promote equality and excellence in the field of computer science and AI, as well as to increase the accessibility of master's studies developing advanced digital skills and promote the growth of higher-level skills, equality and diversity in computer science.
 Converging towards gender equality in ICT fields in EU and the socioeconomic status of the applicant are factors that will be taken into account in the selection process but everyone is welcome to apply regardless their gender and/or socioeconomic situation
 This call covers the cohorts 2025-2027 and 2026-2028.
 2. Characteristics of support 
 The scholarship will be awarded to persons (hereinafter referred to as applicants) who are citizens of the European Union, listed EEA countries or of countries associated to Digital Europe Programme and who are currently studying in the AI4CI project master's degree program “AI4CI Master” at “EETAC” in Castelldefels, Spain; as well as those students who have already been pre-admitted to the “AI4CI Master” (2026-2027) and are expected to complete their enrolment in the coming weeks and those who will be admitted to the “AI4CI Master” for the course 2027-2028.
 This call offers 4 different support modalities , as described below. Applicants may apply for a combination of different support modalities. However, regardless of the combination of modalities requested, the maximum aggregate scholarship amount that may be awarded to any eligible student is 4.500€.
 The maximum amount specified for each modality applies only to that specific modality. Therefore, while different modalities may be combined, the total scholarship amount awarded to any individual student shall not exceed 4.500€. Consequently, no student may receive the maximum amount available under all four modalities simultaneously.
 2.1 Reimbursement of tuition fees 
 Reimbursement of tuition fees includes: 
 The enrollment tuition costs for the full master's program which must be paid before the end of the project.
 Administrative and support fees.
 The cost of issuance of the official title (if paid before the end of the project)
 Each EU beneficiary can be reimbursed up to a maximum of 3.400€. Supporting documentation for the costs incurred will be required.
 2.2 Contribution to living and transportation expenses 
 The scholarship supports living and/or transportation expenses. In particular, it covers a monthly allowance of 100 € for a maximum of 6 months between the resolution of the concession and the end of the project.
 Each beneficiary can receive a maximum of 600€. Supporting documentation for the costs incurred will be required towards reimbursement purposes.
 2.3 Contribution to expenses for mobility stays related to the master program 
 The scholarship supports expenses for in person mobility stays not covered by the Erasmus+ Program related to the AI4CI master program. They must be incurred while the student is enrolled in the program and before the end of the project.
 In particular, it supports living, transportation and accommodation expenses related to study collaboration visit to another institution, academic stay at another institution for the master thesis or attendance to courses taught at another university within the framework of the master program.
 Each beneficiary can receive a maximum of 500€. Supporting documentation for the costs incurred will be required towards reimbursement purposes.
 2.4 Other study-related expenses 
 The scholarship supports expenses for the purchase of hardware and/or software necessary to study; for the acquisition of additional training or information sources, improvement of the necessary competencies and for other study-related expenses. The maximum amount for this modality is up to 1.100€.
 3. Requirements for applicants 
 1. Candidates must have been already admitted to the AI4CI master at UPC EETAC or applied to be admitted for the academic year. This means that to be considered for the scholarship, applicants must apply concurrently to the master's program for the cohort 2026-2028 or be already enrolled in the program from the cohort 2025-2027.
 2. Being a full-time degree-seeking student in the AI4CI master's degree program (corresponding to 30 ECTS per semester).
 3. To be an EU citizen or a citizen of one of the listed EEA countries or of one of the countries associated to Digital Europe Programme – provide a copy of the identity document indicating nationality;
 4. For modality 2.2, having monthly rental expenses of at least 200€ or living at a distance of UPC Castelldefels of at least 20 km.
 5.For modality 2. 3, the expenses have to be related to the AI4CI master program.
 6. For modality 2.4 a justification letter together with the corresponding quotation(s) dated within the previous 15 days to the application and final related invoices and proof of payments.
 4. Applications 
 Applications may be submitted according to the following cut-off dates, provided that the maximum available budget has not been exhausted:
 29 th September 2026 (23:59h Brussels time).
 5 th February 2027 (23:59h Brussels time).
 5 th July 2027 (23:59h Brussels time).
 The application must be submitted through the UPC Electronic Office filling in the UPC-AI4CI scholarships form. The link is as follows: https://seuelectronica.upc.edu/ .
 The following documentation has to be attached to the application form:
 Cover letter stating the following: presentation of the candidate detailing their academic merits, the motivation and plans, how the received scholarship will be used, how it will contribute to the student’s upskilling in advanced digital skills, and the description of their socioeconomic situation (personal, social, economic, work, etc.) that may be relevant to obtaining the scholarship (mandatory for all modalities);
 Documentary evidence of the situations described in the previous point (mandatory for all modalities);
 A copy of the identity document showing the date of birth and nationality of the applicant (mandatory for all modalities);
 For modality 2.2 also provide documentary evidence of meeting the rental or distance requirements established in point 3.4.
 For modality 2.3 also provide information about the mobility stay, letter explaining the purpose and relationship with the master program and budget.
 For modality 2.4 also provide information about the hardware or software purpose of study plus a quotation dated within the previous 15 days to the application and the corresponding invoices and proof of payments. The same will apply with regard to the acquisition of additional or information sources towards the improvement of the necessary competencies or other study-related expenses not covered by modalities 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3.
 5. Selection criteria 
 The selection committee (please refer to clause 7) will evaluate the applications taking into account the academic merit of the candidate as well as the gender and socioeconomic disparities in engineering and computer science.
 For modality 2.3, the relationship of the expenses with the AI4CI master program will be checked.
 In particular, per each modality, a formula of 8 points based on academic merit and 2 points for gender and socioeconomic situation (1 point if female and 1 point if last year annual income has been less than 21.000€ per year) for a total of 10 points will be assigned to each candidate based on the information candidates provide to the committee. Both the master's program application documents and the additional documentation provided for this scholarship application will be taken into account.
 Applications that fulfill the eligibility criteria but are not awarded because of budget limitations will be included in a reserve list (one per each modality). In case one of the awarded candidates can’t accept or refuses the scholarship or loses the financial support, the first candidate in the corresponding reserve list will be automatically re-considered for assessment.
 6. Resolution 
 Applications for modalities 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3 will be continuously assessed.
 Within 5 working days after the reception of applications, the selection committee assesses the received applications, their suitability, award points according to the criteria set out in clause 5 and thus rank the applicants. The selection committee selects the best-ranked applicants, but only those who fully meet the Scholarship requirements described in this call.
 Scholarship resolutions related to this call will be published through UPC’s Electronic Notice Board ( https://seuelectronica.upc.edu/ca/etauler/e-tauler ), “e-Tauler”. and will be communicated to all candidates by the selection committee by e-mail on the same day the resolutions are published. All information about awarded scholarships will be published at the UPC-AI4CI Scholarship website.
 7. Payment conditions 
 Payments related to each modality will be done according to the following schedule, namely:
 1. Awarded students coming from the cohort 2025-2027:
 1st Instalment: 21st October 2026.
 2 nd Instalment: 29 th February 2027.
 2 nd Instalment: 30 th July 2027.
 2. Awarded students coming from the cohort 2026-2028:
 1 st Instalment: 29 th February 2027.
 2 nd Instalment: 30 th July 2027. 
 8. Selection committee 
 The selection committee will be integrated by the members of the Master’s Committee of the AI4CI master program, which currently are:
 Prof. Cristina Cervelló-Pastor.
 Prof. David Rincón Rivera.
 Prof. Carles Gómez Montenegro.
 9. Obligations for applicants 
 Students who have received Scholarships, within 5 working days upon notification, must present to the selection committee the following documents:
 a. A signed scholarship award agreement, which also specifies the consent to the processing of the student's personal data, for scholarship management and marketing purposes and a series of legal obligations that apply to students receiving the support such as respect of ethics, record-keeping, etc.
 b. Provide the bank details necessary for the transfer of the scholarship.
 c. Provide a written declaration, justifying the absence of EU double funding in forms of scholarships.
 d. Document demonstrating that the applicant has successfully completed a minimum of 22.5 ECTS per semester (~75 %).
 10. Right of appeal 
 Students have the right to appeal about the results of the assessment, presenting aspects that they consider inappropriate in their assessment, factual errors in the assessment of the data provided. In the case of an appeal, the following procedure shall apply:
 ·Appeals are accepted by the study programme committee within 10 working days f

beneficiaryAdministration: The Joint Call follows a two-stage application and evaluation procedure.
 Pre-proposals must be submitted electronically through the FOREST Electronic Submission and Evaluation System (ESES). They will undergo a formal eligibility check by the Call Office, national/regional eligibility checks by the relevant Research Funding Organisations, and scientific evaluation by an independent International Expert Panel.
 Following the first-stage evaluation, selected consortia will be invited to submit full proposals. Full proposals will undergo a further formal and national/regional eligibility check and independent scientific evaluation by the International Expert Panel.
 Final recommendations for funding will be made by the Call Steering Committee on the basis of the scientific evaluation, ranking lists and available national/regional and EU funding.
 Applicants must also comply with the applicable national/regional requirements set out in the Funder Regulations.
description: The FOREST Joint Call 2026 – ForestPathways supports transnational research and innovation activities across the spectrum from fundamental research to applied research and, where appropriate, demonstration activities. Projects are expected to generate new knowledge, develop practical solutions, and contribute to implementation in policy, management or industry contexts, while considering the diversity of forests and the forest-based sector.
 Applicants must select the single topic that best reflects the primary focus of their proposal. Proposals may address multiple topics but will be evaluated and ranked under one primary topic.
 TOPIC 1 – Climate-Resilient Forest Systems: “How forests function and respond to climate change” 
 This topic supports research and innovation addressing the resilience, adaptive capacity, and long-term sustainability of forest ecosystems under changing environmental conditions, including climate change and increasing disturbance pressures. It aims to strengthen the scientific basis for climate-resilient forest systems and support their adaptation and mitigation to climate change, within broader environmental and socioeconomic contexts.
 Proposals should address, where relevant, carbon dynamics measurement, monitoring and assessment of carbon stocks and sinks; adaptation pathways and strategies; forest ecosystem processes and dynamics; disturbance regimes, including wildfires and other abiotic and biotic disturbances, pests and diseases; landscape-level interactions and spatial dynamics; and genetic diversity and adaptive capacity, including assisted migration.
 TOPIC 2 – Adaptive and Multifunctional Forest Management Systems: “How forests should be managed under changing conditions” 
 This topic supports research and innovation focused on the implementation of adaptive and multifunctional forest management systems that enhance resilience, sustainability, and the provision of multiple ecosystem services. It aims to support forest management approaches capable of responding to ecological change, disturbance risks, and evolving environmental, economic, and societal demands.
 Proposals should address, where relevant, silvicultural systems and management approaches supporting resilient and multifunctional forests; sustainable harvesting and wood mobilisation methods; monitoring, assessment and planning tools for adaptive management; integration of forest genetic resources into management strategies; operational, digital and technical innovations; risk reduction and adaptation strategies; and trade-offs and synergies between ecosystem services.
 TOPIC 3 – Timber and Innovative Wood-Based Products: “How wood is transformed into innovative products” 
 This topic supports research and innovation on the development, performance, and uptake of timber and innovative wood-based products contributing to decarbonisation and the circular bioeconomy. It aims to advance the development and market uptake of sustainable wood-based products and systems, supporting the substitution of fossil-based and carbon-intensive materials and contributing to low-carbon construction and manufacturing.
 Proposals should address, where relevant, engineered timber and timber construction systems; high-value wood-based products, chemicals and materials; substitution of fossil-based and other carbon-intensive materials; more sustainable alternatives to polluting wood treatments and processing practices; standardisation, testing and certification; circular and resource-efficient use of wood-based products; innovative use of underutilised softwood and hardwood species; innovative manufacturing technologies; and approaches to increase market demand and consumer acceptance and uptake.
 TOPIC 4 – Forest Value Chains, Markets and Governance: “How forest-based sectors, markets and governance are organised” 
 This topic supports research and innovation strengthening the resilience, sustainability, and functioning of forest-based value chains, markets, and governance systems, supporting the transition towards a sustainable and circular forest-based bioeconomy. It aims to support resilient, sustainable, competitive, and innovative forest-based value chains and governance systems capable of responding to environmental, economic, and societal transitions.
 Proposals should address, where relevant, forest-based value chains and market organisation; innovative business models, economic viability and investment readiness; policy, regulatory and governance instruments; barriers to market uptake and innovation deployment; cascading use, circularity and efficient resource use; skills, labour, education and workforce development; and European resilience in sustainable raw material supply, value chains, local processing capacities and forest-based economies.
 The topics provide strategic direction and facilitate evaluation. They are not exhaustive and do not restrict the submission of innovative or cross-cutting proposals aligned with the overall objectives of the call.

textoPagina:
FORESTPathways brings together 36 research funding organisations from 27 countries to support collaborative research and innovation for resilient forests and sustainable forest-based futures
Entitled FORESTPathways – Building Knowledge and Solutions for Resilient Forests and Sustainable Forest-Based Futures, the call brings together 36 Research Funding Organisations from 27 countries, with an indicative total public funding commitment of up to €40 million, including the European Union co-contribution.
FORESTPathways is an important first step in translating the ambitions of the FOREST Partnership into concrete action. By bringing together funding organisations and research communities across countries and connecting research communities across disciplines and sectors, this first Joint Call creates a unique opportunity to generate the knowledge, innovations and collaborations needed for resilient forests and a sustainable and a sustainable and competitive forest-based sector.
Annex VI – List of research performing beneficiaries of the FOREST Partnership (INFO 07.10.26: ALL RPOs that are not direct beneficiaries/partners of the FOREST Partnership may participate in the Joint Call as applicants without any restriction from this annex. RPOs that are direct beneficiaries/partners of the FOREST Partnership are subject to the restrictions set out in this Annex to ensure a fair and level playing field.)
INFORMATION WEBINAR: A webinar was hosted on 17.09.2026 (10:00 CET) for interested applicants. The webinar provided an overview of relevant aspects of the Call and a short introduction to the submission and evaluation system. The webinar slides and recording are now available here: https://forest-partnership.eu/information-webinar-on-the-forest-partnership-joint-call-2026-forestpathways/
NETWORKING WEBINAR: On 06.10.2026 (10:00 CET) the FOREST partnership organises a networking webinar providing stakeholders a chance to connect and network with each other enabling consortia establishments. Please register here: Registration is now closed. Webinar full.
These FAQs are intended to provide clarification of the published FOREST Joint Call 2026 documentation. They do not replace or amend the Call Announcement or its Annexes, which remain the authoritative sources for the Call requirements. Applicants must also consult the relevant national or regional funding regulations, as additional eligibility conditions may apply.
The Call Announcement does not explicitly restrict research activities to forests located within Europe.
However, proposals must address the objectives and scope of the Joint Call. Where research activities are proposed outside Europe, applicants should clearly demonstrate their relevance to the selected research topic and the objectives of the Partnership.
The eligibility of such activities and associated expenditure is subject to the national or regional funding regulations of the participating Research Funding Organisations. Applicants should therefore consult their relevant funders before submitting a proposal.
The four research topics establish the scope and objectives of the Joint Call. The research areas and examples included in the topic descriptions are intended to illustrate the scope rather than provide an exhaustive list of eligible activities.
Applicants should select the primary topic that best reflects the focus of their proposed research and clearly demonstrate how their proposal addresses its objectives.
The Call Office cannot provide advance approval or scientific assessment of individual research concepts and the respective selection of the call topic. Applicants should also consult the relevant national or regional funding regulations for any additional thematic restrictions.
Additional national or regional restrictions may apply, and applicants should consult Annex IV.
An Associated Partner contributes to project activities without requesting funding from a participating Research Funding Organisation. Associated Partners must meet the requirements set out in the Call Announcement, including providing the relevant commitment letters. They cannot coordinate a proposal or count towards the minimum consortium requirements.
No. The research areas listed under each topic are not intended to be a checklist. Applicants are not required to address every area or a particular number of them.

description: The aim of the call is to support the creation, development and practical validation of scalable solutions that address the documented needs of the Czech cybersecurity ecosystem. Supported projects must combine design or development, at least one pilot deployment or practical validation, evaluation of results and preparation for further use. The call is focused on three thematic areas: 
 The call is focused on three main thematic pillars: 
 • Scalable solutions for the resilience of small and medium-sized enterprises: new or significantly expanded services and tools to protect small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), self-assessment, prioritisation of measures and sector- specific implementation packages.
 • Implementation tools and services for compliance readiness, management and risk management: practical solutions for NIS2, CRA, DORA, supply chain security, cybersecurity management, record-keeping, reporting, secure development, SBOM and vulnerability management.
 • Services and technical solutions for incident preparedness, response and recovery: standardised services, sector-specific scenarios, exercise packages and tools for recovery testing, record-keeping, escalation and reporting.
 Support will be given primarily to projects that aim to deliver solutions with a measurable impact on a wider target group. Analyses alone, general training or documentation without implementation and validation activities are not a priority. Implementation by individual organisations is eligible primarily as a means of piloting the transferability and wider applicability of the results.

 To apply, please complete the submission form on EU SURVEY 
 Applications may be modified as long as the deadline is respected: you will be able to save and come back later on EU Survey. The platform will be automatically closed at the date and time announced, that is November 30th, 2026, at 5:00 pm CET. Applicants will receive an e-mail confirming that their application has been well uploaded on the platform. Shall you not receive the confirmation e-mail, please contact Benjamin Schmidt at bes@energycluster.dk and copy your local contact point. SMEs applying as a consortium should fill in one proposal. One of the involved SMEs will act as a “coordinator” and will be responsible for the submission of the application.
 RENEW BOOSTER Eurocluster innovation mechanism will support projects in the "challenges" call and projects in the "open" call, at least 3 SMEs and up to €60,000 euros per SME.
 Evaluation Process and Criteria 
 All eligible applications will be evaluated by evaluators against the criteria defined in the RENEW-BOOSTER Call Text: Excellence, Impact and Quality and efficiency of implementation. Each criterion is scored from 0 to 10, with a minimum threshold of 6/10 per criterion.
 Indicative timeline:
 Call deadline: 30 November 2026 (17:00 CET)
 Evaluation: December 2026
 Results communication: Mid-January 2027
 Contract signature: End-January 2027
 For full details on the evaluation methodology, scoring, thresholds, and tie-breaking rules, please see the call text 
 Proposals will be eligible only if all the following conditions are met: 
 Applicants must be established in one of the following eligible countries: EU-27 + countries participating in the SMP/COSME strand. 
 Applicants must be SMEs according to the European Union definition of SMEs: the formal definition is available here and the SME self-assessment questionnaire is available here .
 Applications must address either the Challenge Call or the Open Call, as described in the Call Text. For applications submitted under the Challenge Call, detailed descriptions of the challenges can be found here or in the EUSurvey submission form.
 Applications must be written in English (applications partially written in another language are not eligible) and must not exceed the maximum number of characters stated in each text box of the pre-defined template available on the submission platform;
 Applications must be submitted through EU Survey 
 SMEs may apply individually to the Challenge Call (Strand A). For the Open Call (Strand B), SMEs may apply either individually or as part of a consortium of up to 3 SMEs.
 Each SME may submit a maximum of one application under Strand A and one application under Strand B, whether applying individually or as part of a consortium. Applications submitted under both strands must address different activities and must not result in double funding. Any SME submitting more than one application to the same strand will be automatically disqualified.
 No annexes can be submitted other than the ones demanded on the EU Survey platform.
 Every applicant organisation needs to be registered on the EU F&T Portal and have a 9-digit Participant Identification Code (PIC). Please find all information PIC number. 
 This call requires private co-funding. Further information can be found here on page 5-7.
 At least 10% of funded SMEs should come from countries or regions other than those represented in the consortium; Denmark, Norway, Poland, France, Bulgaria and Spain.
description: The two calls will be structured through two distinct funding strands. It is reminded that the cumulative maximum FSTP support per SME under the whole set of RENEW-BOOSTER calls is EUR 60,000. An SME may submit a maximum of one application per strand, whether applying individually or as part of a consortium. Consequently, an SME may submit one application under Strand A and one application under Strand B, provided that the proposed activities are distinct and no double funding occurs.
 Strand A (Challenge-driven) follows a two-step process linked to predefined industrial challenges. In Step 1, up to three SMEs per challenge receive €10,000 (with minimum 20% private co-funding) to develop and validate a proof of concept (TRL 6-7). After evaluation and a final pitch, one SME per challenge advances to Step 2 and receives €50,000 (with minimum 40% co-funding) to further develop and scale the solution (TRL 8–9).
 Strand B (Open Call) follows a single-stage selection process. SMEs apply bottom-up and can request up to €10,000, €30,000, or €60,000 depending on project maturity, with increasing private co-funding requirements. Projects run up to six months.
 Find more here: call text

furtherInformation: The RENEW-BOOSTER project aims at driving innovation and industrialization in three critical sectors that are vital for Europe’s green transition and energy security: Photovoltaics (PV), Offshore Wind Energy, and the associated Energy Networks. At the core of RENEW-BOOSTER is the Accelerator, providing tailored support for SMEs to identify opportunities and develop solutions, strengthening their role in the renewable energy value chain and enhancing resilience.
 The project aligns with Europe’s strategic priorities, including reducing critical raw material dependency (Critical Raw Materials Act), advancing climate goals (Green Deal), and supporting re-industrialization (Net Zero Industry Act). RENEW-BOOSTER aims to empower SMEs and accelerate Europe’s twin green and digital transitions.
