beneficiaryAdministration: Applications must be submitted electronically via the F6S platform: https://www.f6s.com/nostradamus-open-call-1/apply by 02 December 2026 at 17:00 CET .
 All Open Call #1 documents are available for download at: https://nostradamus-project.eu/open-call-1/
 Evaluation Workflow: 
 Admissibility & Eligibility Check: Verification of submission criteria, official templates, language (English), single submission rules, country eligibility (EU Member States & Horizon Europe Associated Countries), and applicant eligibility (individual SMEs/start-ups/small mid-caps or 2-partner consortia).
 External Remote Expert Evaluation: Each eligible proposal is reviewed independently by two external experts against 4 criteria: Alignment (score 0–5), Excellence (score 0–5), Impact (score 0–5), and Implementation (score 0–5). Thresholds: min. 3/5 per criterion, min. 12/20 overall. 
 Consensus & Ranking: Expert review panel establishes a consensus report and topic ranking lists (one list per topic, 5 in total). 
 Online Interviews: The top 3 ranked proposals per topic undergo a 30-minute pitch and Q&A session with an Interview committee to finalize scores and ranking. 
 Final Selection & Contracting: Selection of 5 sub-projects (guaranteeing min. 1 project per topic T1–T5) followed by formal KYC verification and Sub-Grant Agreement signature.
description: NOSTRADAMUS Open Call #1 invites system actors and innovators (SMEs, start-ups, small mid-caps, RTOs, end-user organisations) to design, develop, test, and validate multi-functional, open-source digital applications for farm decision-making and agribusiness .
 Selected Third Parties will build upon the NOSTRADAMUS data infrastructure - including multi-dimensional Open Data Cubes, Analysis Ready Data (ARD) Earth Observation pipelines, real-time IoT Observatory streams, and socio-economic datasets - to deliver data-driven tools that optimize agricultural inputs (water, fertilizers, pesticides), improve energy balance, and enhance production resilience in cereal-based agricultural systems.
 The call covers 5 designated topics: 
 Topic 1 (T1): Sustainable crop production and optimisation of cereal-based systems under changing climate and soil conditions. 
 Topic 2 (T2): Nutrient and soil health management, integrating soil fertility indicators, organic matter dynamics, and precision fertilisation models. 
 Topic 3 (T3): Water resource efficiency and drought resilience, using Early Warning System outputs and IoT-based soil moisture monitoring. 
 Topic 4 (T4): Smart and predictive pest and disease management to support the EU objective of reducing pesticide dependency. 
 Topic 5 (T5): Open topic (integrated, cross-domain decision-support applications combining at least two topics T1–T4). 
 Awarded Third Parties must participate in a 12-month 4-Sprint program (Training, Design, Development & Validation, Demonstration & Assessment), physically demonstrate their application at 1 primary NOSTRADAMUS pilot site (DE, RS, CH, SI, or CY), deliver at least 1 user training session, release their source code as open-source, and author an EIP-AGRI Practice Abstract.

beneficiaryAdministration: Article 2
 Eligibility Criteria 
 Students enrolled in DIGISOC are eligible to apply for a scholarship only if they meet all of the following criteria:
 1. DIGISOC Students with EU Citizenship or Citizenship from one of the DEP Associates Countries 
 2. Students who are enrolled in the second year of the DIGISOC programme for academic year 2026/2027. 
 3. DIGISOC Students who have received at least 60 credits for DIGISOC programme courses and completed all courses in which they were enrolled. 
 Article 3
 Application process and period for the academic year 2026/2027 
 The deadline to submit the applications for the DIGISOC scholarship is 14 th December 2026 at 23.59 pm (CET – Central Europe Time).
 Applicants are required to upload the necessary documents as listed below on the DIGISOC OpenOlat platform at the following link: 
 https://lms.uibk.ac.at/auth/RepositoryEntry/5831590270/CourseNode/113899331829124 
 Applicants are required to upload the following materials in a single folder labeled with the applicant name:
 1) The signed Application Letter ( Annex 1 );
 2) The matriculation number at the University which is issuing this call;
 3) The supporting documentation for all eligibility criteria.
 The application must be in English. Supporting documents may be submitted in English, Italian, German, or Czech; all other languages require certified translations. If the documentation is not sufficient, the Evaluation Committee mayrequest additional information or reject the application.
 Article 4
 Evaluation Committee 
 A joint Evaluation Committee, appointed by the Dean of the Faculty of Law of the Palacký University, reviews all applications and consists of:
 · One representative from each of the three DIGISOC degree awarding universities;
 · At least one DIGISOC student representative;
 The Committee is appointed after the deadline for the application submission and terminates the evaluation process no later than 15 days after the deadline.
 Article 5
 Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure 
 The joint Evaluation Committee will check eligibility criteria and evaluate each application.
 The candidate academic excellence will be evaluated based on the weighted average of grades achieved during academic year 2025/2026 in all DIGISOC courses, calculated and rounded to hundredths (e.g. 28,77) on a 30 points scale according to the DIGISOC grade conversion table. Based on averages, students who have submitted their application will be put in descending order. In case of tie, they will be put on shared place, awarding the higher award.
 To determine the exact amount of the scholarship allocated to each applicant, the joint Evaluation Committee will use the following model:
 · the Student with highest average will be awarded a 2000 EUR scholarship.
 · the Student with second highest average will be awarded a 1750 EUR scholarship.
 · the Student with third highest average will receive a 1500 EUR scholarship.
 · All other students with average above 26,99 will receive a scholarship which corresponds to the result of dividing the call's remaining budget by the number of applications fulfilling the award criteria, but not exceeding 1000 EUR per applicant.
 The joint Evaluation Committee’s judgement is unquestionable.
 The rankings and the exact amount of funding received by each applicant will be published on the DIGISOC website ( https://digitalsociety4innovation.eu/costs-and-scholarships/ ) and the DIGISOC Awarding Universities Websites. This publication has the value of notification.

texto:
es_SortDate: 2026-10-04T00:00:00.000+0000
beneficiaryAdministration: Eligibility Criteria 
 Students enrolled in DIGISOC for the second year are eligible to apply for a scholarship if they meet one or more of the following criteria:
 1. Students with certified disabilities 
 Students with certified disabilities can apply for a DIGISOC scholarship. In the context of this call, and following Article 1 of the European Disability Policy, students with disabilities are considered students who have long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments which, in interaction with various barriers, may hinder their full and effective participation in society on an equal basis with others. Applicants must provide certified medical documentation or proof of a national disability status.
 2. Migrants or refugees 
 Students who are migrants or refugees can apply for funding based on their status. Required proof may include an asylum decision, a residence permit, or confirmation issued by a migration authority.
 3. Students with low socio-economic family conditions 
 Students from families with low socio-economic conditions can apply for funding. Low socio-economic conditions are defined according to the student’s family income. Required proof may include a tax statement, an income certificate, or an official social benefit statement.
 4. Students living in remote areas 
 Students living in a region in the lowest 25% of national population density and/or with no regular access to higher education within a 100 km radius may apply. Required proof is a residence certificate, which will be assessed against infrastructure data based on national statistics.
 Application process and period for the academic year 2026/2027 
 The deadline to submit applications for the DIGISOC scholarships is 10. December 2026 at 23.59 CET (Central European Time).
 Applicants are required to upload the necessary documents listed below on the DIGISOC OpenOlat platform at the following link:
 https://lms.uibk.ac.at/auth/RepositoryEntry/5831590270/CourseNode/114518610654144 
 Applicants are required to upload the following materials in a single folder labelled with the applicant’s name:
 · The signed Application Letter (Annex 1);
 · The applicant’s registration number (Matrikelnummer) at the University of Innsbruck;
 · The supporting documentation for each claimed eligibility criterion, issued by a responsible authority or accredited expert.
 · The Data Protection and Consent Declaration (Annex 2).
 The application must be in English. Supporting documents may be submitted in English, Italian, German, or Czech; documents in other languages require certified translations. If the documentation is insufficient, the Evaluation Committee may request additional information or reject the application.
 By submitting the application and signing Annex 1, the applicant expressly confirms that the application has been submitted completely and correctly and that all information and supporting documents are accurate and complete. Incomplete applications may be excluded from the selection procedure.
 Evaluation Committee 
 A joint Evaluation Committee, appointed by the Study Coordinator (Studienbeauftragter) of the Faculty of Economics and Statistics of the University of Innsbruck, reviews all applications and consists of:
 · One representative from each of the three DIGISOC degree-awarding universities;
 · At least one student representative from the University of Innsbruck;
 · Disability officer at the University of Innsbruck.
 The Committee is appointed after the deadline for application submission and completes the evaluation process no later than 15 days after the deadline.
 Awarding Criteria and Evaluation Procedure 
 The joint Evaluation Committee will evaluate each application and award points based on the following criteria:
 1. Students with certified disabilities 
 Applicants will be awarded points on the basis of the severity and impact of their condition, ranging from 5 points for a comparatively less impactful disability to 10 points for a very serious disability.
 2. Migrants or refugees 
 Applicants will be awarded points as follows: 
 a. 10 points for refugee status; 
 b. 10 points for migrant status with less than 5 years in the current country of residence; 
 c. 5 points for migrant status with 5 or more years in the current country of residence.
 3. Low socio-economic family condition 
 Applicants will be awarded 10 points if their family income falls within the first quartile (Q1), i.e. within the 25% of the population with the lowest incomes in their country of origin. Applicants will be awarded 5 points if their family income falls between the first and second quartile (Q2), i.e. within the range defined by the median income and Q1 in their country of origin. The reference fiscal year is the year preceding the year in which the application is submitted.
 4. Remote areas 
 Applicants will be awarded 5 points for residence in a remote area. An additional 5 points will be awarded if the student’s residence is in a remote area with no regular access to higher education within a 100 km radius.
 All applications will be ranked on the basis of the sum of points obtained across the four criteria. Each application can obtain a maximum of 30 points.
 To determine the exact amount of the scholarship allocated to each applicant, the joint Evaluation Committee will use a proportional point-based model:
 · Total funds available are divided by the sum of all points awarded across valid applications;
 · This determines a value per point (EUR/point);
 · Each applicant receives funding according to their own score, up to the maximum of EUR 3,000.00.
 The decision of the joint Evaluation Committee is final, subject to the appeal procedure set out in Article 6.
 The exact amount of funding and its composition awarded to each applicant will be published via the Learning Management System OpenOLAT. This publication constitutes as notification.

destinationDetails: Eligibility Criteria 
 Students enrolled in DIGISOC for the second year are eligible to apply for a scholarship if they meet one or more of the following criteria:
 1. Students with certified disabilities 
 Students with certified disabilities can apply for a DIGISOC scholarship. In the context of this call, and following Article 1 of the European Disability Policy, students with disabilities are considered students who have long-term physical, mental, intellectual or sensory impairments which, in interaction with various barriers, may hinder their full and effective participation in society on an equal basis with others. Applicants must provide certified medical documentation or proof of a national disability status.
 2. Migrants or refugees 
 Students who are migrants or refugees can apply for funding based on their status. Required proof may include an asylum decision, a residence permit, or confirmation issued by a migration authority.
 3. Students with low socio-economic family conditions 
 Students from families with low socio-economic conditions can apply for funding. Low socio-economic conditions are defined according to the student’s family income. Required proof may include a tax statement, an income certificate, or an official social benefit statement.
 4. Students living in remote areas 
 Students living in a region in the lowest 25% of national population density and/or with no regular access to higher education within a 100 km radius may apply. Required proof is a residence certificate, which will be assessed against infrastructure data based on national statistics.
 Application process and period for the academic year 2026/2027 
 The deadline to submit applications for the DIGISOC scholarships is 10. December 2026 at 23.59 CET (Central European Time).
 Applicants are required to upload the necessary documents listed below on the DIGISOC OpenOlat platform at the following link:
 https://lms.uibk.ac.at/auth/RepositoryEntry/5831590270/CourseNode/114518610654144 
 Applicants are required to upload the following materials in a single folder labelled with the applicant’s name:
 · The signed Application Letter (Annex 1);
 · The applicant’s registration number (Matrikelnummer) at the University of Innsbruck;
 · The supporting documentation for each claimed eligibility criterion, issued by a responsible authority or accredited expert.
 · The Data Protection and Consent Declaration (Annex 2).
 The application must be in English. Supporting documents may be submitted in English, Italian, German, or Czech; documents in other languages require certified translations. If the documentation is insufficient, the Evaluation Committee may request additional information or reject the application.
 By submitting the application and signing Annex 1, the applicant expressly confirms that the application has been submitted completely and correctly and that all information and supporting documents are accurate and complete. Incomplete applications may be excluded from the selection procedure.
 Evaluation Committee 
 A joint Evaluation Committee, appointed by the Study Coordinator (Studienbeauftragter) of the Faculty of Economics and Statistics of the University of Innsbruck, reviews all applications and consists of:
 · One representative from each of the three DIGISOC degree-awarding universities;
 · At least one student representative from the University of Innsbruck;
 · Disability officer at the University of Innsbruck.
 The Committee is appointed after the deadline for application submission and completes the evaluation process no later than 15 days after the deadline.

convocatoria: Mission ocean in Slovenian seas — Call for proposals for the provision of financial support to third parties for the implementation of small-scale projects under the RISTANC project
texto:
es_SortDate: 2026-09-28T00:00:00.000+0000
beneficiaryAdministration: 1. Eligible applicants 
 The call is open to a wide range of applicants, including innovators, researchers, artists, individuals, representatives of civil society, non-governmental organisations, local communities, informal and local initiatives, start-up companies, schools, research teams and other individuals and organisations whose projects contribute to achieving the objectives of the call. The following entities are eligible to apply for the call:
 public and private legal entities (e.g. non-governmental organisations, associations, institutes, commercial companies, local communities, research organisations, educational institutions, social enterprises and other legal entities),
 natural persons.
 Additional conditions:
 If the applicant applies as a (public or private) legal entity, the registered office or business address of the applicant must be located in a Member State of the European Union, its overseas countries or territories (OCTs), or in a country associated with the Horizon Europe programme. If the applicant applies as a natural person, they must hold a permanent residence address within the European Union Member States.
 Applications may be submitted individually or in partnership. If the applicant includes partners in the project implementation, they remain the project lead and responsible for the project implementation, including financial responsibility for its execution.
 Each (public or private) legal or natural person may participate in only one application under this call, either as an applicant or as a partner. In the event that the same applicant submits or participates in multiple applications, only the first application submitted will be considered, and the remaining applications will not be processed.
 The proposed project must address one or more of the challenges set out in the call, and the planned activities must be implemented in the Slovenian territorial sea, including the coast,or contribute to addressing challenges in this area.
 The selected applicant must have settled all outstanding tax liabilities and, where relevant, social security contributions before signing the funding agreement. The contracting authority will verify compliance with this condition prior to the signing of the contract. If the verification reveals that the condition has not been met, the contract shall not be concluded; the project may be rejected and financial support awarded to the next highest-ranked project.
 Consortium partners of the RISTANC project are not eligible to apply for this call, either as (public or private) legal entities or as natural persons.
 Informal or local initiatives may apply through a natural person acting as the applicant, who shall be responsible for the project implementation.
 The project or activities for which financial support is claimed under this call must not be funded by other European, national, or local public sources. The applicant shall provide a declaration to this effect in the application documentation.
 Applicants who are personally, professionally, economically, or otherwise linked to the RISTANC consortium partners must disclose their connections.
 The valid Slovenian Maritime Spatial Plan is used to define the geographical scope of this call.
 2. How to apply 
 The application for funding, together with all required attachments in PDF format, shall be submitted by email to the address ristanc-funding@zrs-kp.si . In the email subject line, please state: RISTANC – application for the call [name of applicant]. The application may be submitted in Slovenian or English.
 The application submission deadline is from 28 September 2026 to 28 November 2026 until 23:59 (CET).
 An application shall be considered timely if the email is sent by the deadline specified in the call. The application must include a completed and signed application form, including the required annexes as defined in the application form.
 An information seminar will be organised for all (potential) applicants, which will take place on Tuesday, 6 October 2026, on the Zoom online platform. Applicants may send questions regarding the call to the email address ristanc-funding@zrs-kp.si no later than 31 October 2026. Answers to questions will be published on the project RISTANC website and will form an integral part of the tender documentation.
 3. Selection procedure and project evaluation 
 The opening of Applications is not public . Following the expiry of the application submission deadline, the expert commission shall first verify the timeliness and formal completeness of the Applications received. If the commission finds that an Application is formally incomplete (e.g. unclear administrative data in Sections A and B; this does not apply to Section C), it may request the applicant to supplement it. Supplementing the Application is intended to rectify formal deficiencies and must not affect the project content, the requested amount of financial support, or its evaluation. The deadline for supplementation is five (5) working days from receipt of the call, which the commission shall send only once. If the applicant fails to supplement the Application within the prescribed period or if the supplementation is inadequate, the Application shall be rejected . 
 Only complete applications shall be admitted to the evaluation process. An application shall be considered complete if: it contains all required application forms, evidence, declarations, and annexes specified in this call for applications; it was submitted within the prescribed deadline and in the manner specified in the call; all mandatory information in the application forms has been completed; it is signed by the applicant's legal representative (or an authorised person) if the applicant is applying as a (public or private) legal entity; it is signed by a natural person if the applicant is applying as a natural person. Applications that do not meet all the above conditions will be considered incomplete.
 Projects are evaluated by a five-member expert commission on the basis of pre-determined and published criteria. The applicant will receive the Evaluation criteria together with the application form. A priority list of projects is established on the basis of the scores achieved.
 Before the evaluation starts, the expert commission adopts a formal decision on the prevention and management of conflicts of interest. Each commission member signs a declaration of confidentiality and absence of conflict of interest. A member with an actual or perceived conflict of interest with an applicant or its partners does not assess, discuss or rank the application concerned; such cases are recorded in the evaluation minutes.
 To be eligible for funding, a project must achieve at least 55 points in the evaluation.
 Where two or more applications obtain the same total score, priority is given to the application with the higher score under criterion 1 and, if still equal, under criterion 4.
 The highest-rated applicants will be invited to a short oral presentation of the project idea, which is expected to take place on 10 December 2026, either in person or remotely. The purpose of the oral presentation is to provide a brief overview of the project idea and an opportunity for further clarification before the final project selection decision is made. No new content may be introduced and the requested amount may not be increased. The final scores are confirmed solely on the basis of the published evaluation criteria, and the final priority list is recorded in the evaluation minutes.
 In the event that no submitted project reaches the minimum funding threshold or is selected for financing, the call organiser reserves the right to repeat and adapt the call.
 4.Evaluation criteria 
 Applications are evaluated against the following award criteria (maximum score): 1. Consistency of the proposed project with the challenges set out in Call, clarity and appropriateness of the main project objective, and appropriateness of the approach for monitoring its achievement (20); 2. Quality and feasibility of the implementation plan and timeline (20); 3. Degree of innovation and originality of the proposed project idea (10); 4. Expected impact of the project, including the impact on target groups (20); 5. Sustainability plan for results (10); 6. Competencies and experience of the applicant in relation to the submitted project and the content of the call (10); 7. Cost-effectiveness of the budget (10). Total: 100 points.
 5. Notification of results and funding agreement 
 Applicants will be notified of the results of the call by 15 December 2026 at the latest. The results of the call, including a description of the selected projects, award dates, project durations and the legal names and countries of the recipients, will be published on the RISTANC website and on the F&T portal.
 The selected applicant shall be deemed not to accept the funding if, within 10 days of receipt of the selection notification, they fail to provide written confirmation of acceptance of the funds (written confirmation via the email address provided in the application form is also valid). In the event of withdrawal by the selected applicant, funding may be approved for the next applicant on the priority list.
 6. Legal protection 
 No appeal or objection is admissible against the substantive decision, assessment, and evaluation of projects by the expert commission. An applicant may lodge an objection solely in the event of suspected procedural errors (breach of the public call procedure). An objection shall be lodged with the call organiser within 8 days of receipt of the notification of the outcome of the call. The head of the procedure shall decide on the objection within 15 days of its receipt. If the objection is upheld and a procedural error is identified, the challenged decision on selection or non-selection shall be set aside, and the applicant's application shall be returned to the expert commission for reconsideration and a new decision. The commission must rectify the identified error in the reopened procedure.
description: 1. Purpose of the call 
 The call is published as part of the implementation of the European RISTANC project, which is financed by the Horizon Europe programme. The project contributes to the implementation of the EU Mission “Restore Our Ocean and Waters by 2030”, with a focus on the Slovenian marine area, which is prt of the cross-border North Adriatic region.
 2. Key challenges 
 The call encourages projects that contribute to addressing the following thematic areas:
 The establishment and management of moorings in the Slovenian sea for recreational and tourist vessels that prevent damage to marine seabed habitats,
 The planning and implementation of interventions in the coastal zone of the Slovenian sea that harmonise the various needs and interests of people and the environment,
 Other measures in the Slovenian sea area (and potentially beyond) that contribute to the objectives of the EU Mission “Restore Our Ocean & Waters”, such as reducing pollution in the marine environment (including plastic and other waste), the conservation and restoration of marine ecosystems, and the development of a sustainable blue economy .

convocatoria: Financial support for participation in AI SECRETT master programme’s extracurricular educational activities (First edition). Call identifier: AI SECRETT-FSTP-CALL-01-2026.
texto:
es_SortDate: 2026-10-01T00:00:00.000+0000
beneficiaryAdministration: The Call has 5 distinct cut-off dates. All submitted applications by each deadline will be evaluated jointly and awarded until funding resources are available. The AI-SECRETT consortium reserves the right of integrating the funding budget with an extra allocation, up to twice the initially allocated amount. A same natural person can apply multiple times at different cut-off dates but can receive the financial benefits of this Call only once.
 Applications will only be possible electronically and exclusively managed through the GoodGrants TM platform (https://aisecrett.grantplatform.com/) by filling in a form and attaching the required documentation.
 Evaluation of received applications will be done by a special committee established at the Funding Body, Universidad de Valencia (UVEG). Each application will be evaluated from the perspectives of admissibility, eligibility, and merit.
 Admissibility conditions will be that an electronic application has been received on or before the latest cut-off date, completed in all its parts, and with all required attachments, exclusively through the GoodGrants TM platform. Incomplete applications or submitted by other means will be discarded and proposed for resubmission at the next cut-off date.
 To pass the admissibility check, all applicants must submit at least:
 - A signed application form;
 - Their CV in Europass format (see https://europass.europa.eu/en/create-europass-cv );
 - A motivation letter (explicitly stating employment status and financial need);
 - Any documentation supporting disadvantaged background and/or priority categories (where applicable);
 - Signed declarations (no conflict of interest, double funding, etc.) using the templates available on the GoodGrants TM platform;
 - A proof of enrolment or acceptance in the AI-SECRETT master’s programme, dated not earlier than the opening of this Call and not yet finalised by the chosen cut-off date;
 - A proof of enrolment or acceptance in at least one extracurricular activity of the AI-SECRETT project, dated not earlier than the opening of this Call and not yet finalised by the chosen cut-off date; and
 - An indicative cost breakdown (travel, accommodation, registration/participation fees, other costs).
 All the above documentation must be provided in English language. Unofficial translations are allowed in case of submission of documents that are natively not in English, but the applicant will take the risk and bear the consequences of any misinterpretation during the evaluation process.
 Eligibility conditions will be that
 - The applicants must be natural persons and nationals of an eligible country for the Call (see Further information below);
 - They must not be subject to restrictive measures or other disqualifying conditions according to the EU or national legislation in their country;
 - They cannot receive double funding for the same operation;
 - They must not be in a situation of conflict of interest with UVEG or any other AI-SECRETT partner.
 Eligible applications received until the same cut-off date will be scored using the following criteria (max. 100 points):
 Criterion 
 Description 
 Max score 
 Excellence and relevance 
 Academic/professional background and fit with AI‑SECRETT vertical industries (*)
 30 
 Motivation and expected impact 
 Learning objectives, career impact, clarity of plan
 25 
 Financial need 
 Economic situation and justification of requested support
 25 
 European added value 
 Cross‑border dimension, diversity contribution
 20 
 (*) Agri-Food, Cultural and Creative Industries, Energy and Environment, Housing, Manufacturing, Mobility and Transport, and Non-Touristic Services.
 No minimum thresholds or weighting will be applied. In case of equal scores, the following priority rules will be adopted, in the same order:
 Applicants enrolled in more than one extracurricular activity.
 Applicants from countries not full members of the AI‑SECRETT consortium.
 Applicants from regions with average income below 75% of the EU average.
 Female applicants (if merit equivalent).
 The maximum financial support per beneficiary is:
 EUR 5 000 (five thousand Euros / 00) 
 The awarded amount is calculated on the basis of:
 - Actual and justified travel costs,
 - Actual and justified accommodation costs,
 - Actual and documented registration/participation fees,
 - Actual, justified and documented other costs.
 as reported in the indicative cost breakdown (see above). The Selection Committee may cap specific cost items if considered excessive or not in line with typical market prices for the location and period.
 The awarded amount will be adjusted to the recipient’s country of origin following the latest adjustment coefficients of the Marie Skłodowska Curie actions available (see e.g. https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/horizon/wp-call/2023-2024/wp-2-msca-actions_horizon-2023-2024_en.pdf ).
 Eligible expenses are those realised after the date of submission of the respective application .
 The scheme reimburses up to 50% of total eligible costs, within the 5 000 EUR cap, so that the minimum number of supported beneficiaries with available resources (equally distributed across two yearly editions of this Call) will be at least 240.
description: The procedure follows the principles of:
 transparency,
 equal treatment,
 confidentiality,
 absence of conflict of interest.
 Admissibility and eligibility checks precede scoring; only eligible applications will be scored.
 Eligible proposals are ranked by total score within the available budget.
 The final award decision is endorsed by UVEG. All applicants will receive a written justification for the decision, with terms to appeal.
 Selected beneficiaries will be requested to sign a Financial Support Agreement (see text here: https://aisecrett.eu/bid-to-our-call/FSA) specifying the supported activity, eligible costs, maximum amount, payment schedule and reporting obligations.
 Failure to sign within the indicated timeframe may lead to loss of the grant by the autonomous decision of UVEG.
 Payments will be made by UVEG, normally after participation in the activity and approval of the beneficiary report and cost statement. Details are provided in the individual Financial Support Agreement (including e.g. the possibility of small prefinancing in justified cases).

titulo: Supporting Ukrainian artists and cultural organisations to co-create/showcase
convocatoria: ZMINA:Resilience. Second call for co-creation funding of international cooperation projects
texto:
es_SortDate: 2026-10-05T00:00:00.000+0000
beneficiaryAdministration: The IZOLYATSIA Foundation (UA) and Malý Berlín (SK), together with Trans Europe Halles (SE), announce the second call for proposals for the co-creation funding of international cooperation projects. 
 The objective of the call is to support co-creation between Ukrainian artists and cultural organisations and their peers from Creative Europe countries on the topic of resilience.
 Funding will be available for co-creation projects involving at least one Ukrainian partner and a partner from another Creative Europe participating country. Each partner is expected to play a role of comparable weight in the project — whether through creative input, management responsibilities, or audience development. All creative sectors are eligible, with the exception of the audio-visual sector. Each co-creation project must include a public presentation in the locality of every participating partner.
 Purpose of the call: 
 To develop and present an international co-creation on the topic of resilience, in any artistic/cultural sector except audio-visual.
 To carry out at least two local presentations (one/locality, including in Ukraine)
 Budget: 
 — Total funding available 187,500€
 — Amounts per grant: Up to 25,000€, covering up to 90% of project costs.
 — Applicants are expected and required to provide the rest of the total project budget as a contribution.
 — Expected number of grants 7-10
 Eligible applicants: 
 Organisations active in the field of arts and culture established in a Creative Europe country ( EU countries , non-EU countries ). For Ukraine, they must be registered in a zone effectively controlled by the Ukrainian government . Projects must include at least two partners from at least two countries, of which one is Ukraine. Individual artists and freelancers cannot apply directly; they must take part through an eligible organisation acting as a project partner.
 List of activities that are eligible for financial support:
 — All activities necessary for the co-creation project implementation and development.
 — Presentation of the co-creation in the locality of each project partner.
 — Travel related to organisational, rehearsal, artistic, presentation purposes.
 Duration of the project: 
 — project duration period: up to 7 months within the indicative implementation window of February–August 2027;
 — earliest start of the project after the signature of the grant agreement.
 Technical eligibility criteria: 
 all required attachments (as described in the Application Procedure below) are uploaded to the platform in separate files and in the formats specified for this call;
 all required attachments are uploaded to the platform following standard templates that can be downloaded on the platform;
 all required attachments are readable, accessible, and printable;
 all the project partners meet the eligibility conditions specified for this call;
 the registration of all the project partners meets the conditions specified for this call;
 the application form is complete and contains all the requested information;
 the total subgrant amount requested in the budget is within the maximum subgrant amounts determined for this call;
 the total project partners contribution meets the conditions specified for this call;
 project implementation period is within the project implementation period defined for this call;
 the start of project implementation meets the conditions specified for this call.
 Selection criteria: 
 Relevance: 
 — relevance of the project to the objectives of the call;
 — relevance of potential co-creation to act as a basis for intercultural dialogue.
 Quality: 
 — quality of extent to which cross-cutting issues (digital, green, inclusion) are addressed, including barrier-free access to project results;
 — quality of the partnership: the equal importance of the roles played by project partners;
 — quality of scale of engagement, measured by the expected audience size and number of local presentations.
 Impact: 
 — Impact and the sustainability of the project, including plans and possibilities for future presentations of the co-creation.
 Selection procedure: 
 Applications will first undergo a technical eligibility check by the ZMINA:Resilience team to verify that they meet all formal requirements, including admissibility and eligibility criteria. Proposals that pass this stage will then be assigned to two independent evaluators each.
 Evaluators will assign scores to applications. Then, the applications will be rated according to the average score.
 The final selection will be made by the Selection Committee, taking into account geographical, sectoral, and thematic diversity, within the available budget of the call.
 The application budget will be assessed for cost-effectiveness and plausibility, and may be adjusted before the grant agreement is signed. The final grant amount will be determined based on a combination of lump sum units and actual costs incurred: costs such as artist fees, travel, accommodation, and per diems are paid at the fixed unit rates listed under "Eligible costs covered by the grant" below, regardless of the exact amount spent, while costs such as equipment rental, production services, and shipping are reimbursed based on actual costs incurred.
 Due to the volume of applications received, the ZMINA:Resilience project team will not be able to provide individual feedback for selection decisions. All decisions are final.
 Application Procedure 
 — Applications must be submitted via the IZOLYATSIA online platform no later than 04.12.2026, 23:59 Kyiv time / 22:49 Central European Time on https://platform.izolyatsia.org/en/contest/zmina-resilience-cocreation-two .
 — Applicant: The application shall be submitted by a single representative of the consortium/project partners (Lead Applicant).
 Required Documents: 
 The application form and budget (completed directly on the platform),
 Supporting documents regarding capacity, eligibility, and admissibility. The following must be uploaded to the platform in .pdf format separately for each partner:
 A scanned copy of the Letter of Guarantee , completed and signed by the head of the applicant organization (template available for download on the platform);
 Registration documents for organisation registered in Creative Europe countries other than Ukraine: national registration documents with English translation in case the document is issued in another language.
 Registration documents for organisation from Ukraine: Full Extract from the Unified State Register of Legal Entities, Physical Persons-Entrepreneurs, and Public Formations dated on or after 5 October 2026 - in their original language.
 The current version of the Statutes or equivalent (if mandatory for the legal entity) – all pages: for organisation registered in Creative Europe countries other than Ukraine: with English translation in case the document is issued in another language, for organisation from Ukraine: in their original language.
 Language of application: The application must be submitted in English.
 Support: During the application period, assistance will be provided through Q&A sessions and a dedicated email helpline.
 Subgrant Agreement Template 
 Funding Conditions 
 — Financial support: 70% is disbursed upon signing the grant agreement, and the remaining amount is paid upon submission and approval of the report.
 — Co-financing is mandatory and must be at least 10% of the total project budget.
 — Double funding within the EU budget is not allowed.
 — All costs must be incurred after the grant agreement is signed and within the project implementation period.
 — Compliance with EU branding and visibility requirements is mandatory . 
 Eligible costs covered by the grant include 
 Daily fee for artistic work: 75€/artist/day
 Travel: International: 350€/return trip or Local (e.g. participation in trainings): 65€/return trip 
 Support to green travel (in addition to the travel rate above, for one-way trips over 600km not made by air): 300€ 
 Accommodation & per diem: 75€/overnight 
 Visa cost, if needed: 80€ 
 Shipping/Transport (of equipment), incl. insurance: at cost;
 Supplies & equipment (for equipment depreciation costs only): at cost;
 Services required for project implementation (production, rental of equipment, rental of space for project events, etc.): at cost;
 Communication, marketing and documentation: at cost.
 Management and administration costs: Max. 20% of the overall project budget (grant amount plus own contribution/co-financing combined).
 Estimated dates: 
 — Launch of the Call for Proposals: 5 October 2026
 — Deadline for Submission of Applications: until 23:59 4December 2026 (Kyiv time)
 — Evaluation Period: December 2026
 — Announcement of Results: January 2027
 — Signing of Grant Agreements: February 2027
 — Implementation of Selected Projects: February 2027 – August 2027 (each project runs up to 7 months within this window, depending on its grant agreement signing date)

 To develop and present an international co-creation on the topic of resilience, in any artistic/cultural sector except audio-visual.

 — Applicants are expected and required to provide the rest of the total project budget as a contribution.

 Eligible applicants: 
 Organisations active in the field of arts and culture established in a Creative Europe country ( EU countries , non-EU countries ). titulo: Specialised education programmes or modules in key capacity areas
convocatoria: AI4CI - Fee waivers for Ulm University
texto:
es_SortDate: 2026-10-01T00:00:00.000+0000
beneficiaryAdministration: 1. Aim, Project, Background and Objective 
 The AI4CI project, co-funded by the European Union under Grant Agreement No. 101123524, provides financial support to students enrolled in the continuing education master’s programme “Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries” at Ulm University (UUlm), Germany.
 The objective of this call is to increase accessibility to advanced digital skills education, support up- and reskilling of professionals, and promote diversity and inclusion in computer science education.
 Within this call, up to 80 fee waivers (with a total amount of max. 80.000 EUR), for individual modules in winter term 2026-2027 (October 2026-March 2027) will be awarded.
 A fee waiver covers 80 % of the tuition fee of a module in the AI4CI programme. The module fees range from 585 to 1800 Euros. depending on module size in ECTS and specific characteristics of modules (e.g. inclusion of lab times or high amount of tutoring). Fee waivers therefore range between 468 and 1440 Euros.
 Fee waivers apply only to modules taken in the semester for which the waiver is granted.
 Applicants may apply for fee waivers for multiple modules, provided they are enrolled in these modules.
 2. Eligibility 
 Applicants must fulfil all the following criteria:
 1. Be a citizen of an EU Member State, an EEA country, or a country associated with the Digital Europe Programme ( https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/digital/guidance/list-3rd-country-participation_digital_en.pdf ),
 2. Be admitted and enrolled in the master’s programme Artificial Intelligence for Connected Industries at Ulm University.
 3. Be registered as a student of the programme in winter semester 2026/2027.
 4. Apply only for modules that
 a. are part of the AI4CI curriculum and
 b. can still be credited toward the final grade and degree.
 5. A fee waiver may be granted only once per module per student.
 3. Scope of the Support 
 A maximum of 80 module fee waivers will be awarded in this call.
 Each fee waiver reduces the tuition fee of the respective module by 80 %.
 Fee waivers apply only to the semester in which the module is taken.
 Students may receive multiple fee waivers, provided they apply for different modules and ranking positions allow it.
 4. Application Procedure 
 4.1 Call Announcement 
 By 1 October, all admitted students will receive information about:
 the availability of fee waivers,
 the eligibility requirements,
 the application procedure,
 and the application deadline.
 4.2 Application Deadline 
 Applications must be submitted by 1 December 2026.
 Applicants must submit:
 a completed application form indicating
 other modules they will attend in winter semester 2026-2027, and
 other modules for which a fee waiver is requested.
 proof of nationality.
 consent allowing the programme administration to access relevant student data in the HIS student administration system and the App4Master admission system.
 Applicants may additionally submit supporting documentation relevant to diversity criteria described in Section 7.
 5. Evaluation Procedure 
 Applications will be evaluated by the Study Programme Committee of the AI4CI programme at Ulm University and the corresponding talent scouting team.
 The evaluation will take place within 10 working days after the application deadline.
 Each module application is evaluated independently.
 Applications will be ranked according to the evaluation criteria defined in Section 6 and the tie-breaking and diversity considerations criteria in section 7.
 The highest-ranked module applications will receive a fee waiver.
 All remaining eligible applications will be placed on a reserve list.
 Applicants will be informed about the outcome within five working days after the evaluation.
 6. Evaluation Criteria 
 The fee waiver scheme supports up- and reskilling in advanced AI competencies.
 Applications are evaluated based on the curriculum category of the module.
 Points are assigned as follows:
 Module Area 
 Points 
 A2 Mandatory Area – Artificial Intelligence
 3
 B1 Systems and Networks
 2
 B2 Automatics and Robotics
 2
 B3 Processes and Data Management
 2
 B4 Free Elective Module
 1
 All module areas are defined in the Subject-Specific Study and Examination Regulations of the AI4CI programme (10 June 2025) and its additional documents.
 The maximum score per module application is 3 points.
 7. Tie-Breaking and Diversity Considerations 
 If multiple applications receive the same score, the following criteria will be applied sequentially to determine priority:
 Women and gender minorities
 Applicants with disabilities
 Applicants with family responsibilities or caregiving duties
 Supporting documentation may be provided during the application process.
 If applications remain tied after applying the above criteria, the final ranking will be determined by random draw conducted by the study programme committee and the talent scouting team.
 8. Award and Implementation of the Fee Waiver 
 Students selected for a fee waiver will receive an updated tuition fee notice reflecting the 80 % reduction for the respective module.
 Receiving a fee waiver does not prevent students from applying for other scholarships, unless the conditions of those programmes prohibit it.
 However, double funding from EU sources for the same purpose is not permitted.
 If a student receives additional funding, the student must provide a written declaration confirming the absence of EU double funding.
 If double funding is identified, the fee waiver may be reduced or withdrawn.
 9. Appeals 
 Applicants may submit an appeal only in cases of procedural errors or factual inaccuracies in the evaluation.
 Appeals must:
 be submitted in writing within five working days after notification of the results;
 clearly indicate the alleged procedural error or incorrect data.
 The study programme committee will review the appeal and provide a decision within 10 working days.
 10. Termination of the Fee Waiver 
 The fee waiver may be withdrawn if the student:
 withdraws from the programme,
 takes academic leave,
 transfers to another study programme,
 or violates academic integrity or ethical standards.
 Students may voluntarily withdraw from the fee waiver by submitting a written request.
 Unused funding may be reallocated in a future fee waiver call within the AI4CI project.
 11. Publication of Results 
 The final list of fee waiver recipients will be published no later than 15 December 2026.
 Personal data will be processed and published in accordance with applicable data protection regulations.

convocatoria: LLM-BRIDGE – Venture Incubation Programme - Open Call for Incubators – 2nd Call
texto:
es_SortDate: 2026-09-28T00:00:00.000+0000
beneficiaryAdministration: Proposal submission: 
 All proposals shall be submitted at: https://share.hsforms.com/133VDDomZReqeyGTex0VYRwf4os 
 Proposal template and supporting documents: 
 The proposal template and supporting documents are available at: https://www.llm-bridge.eu/open-calls-2/
 Evaluation process: 
 Eligible proposals will be evaluated by independent external experts, appointed by the LLM-BRIDGE Consortium, to ensure objectivity and impartiality.
 Each proposal will be assessed by at least two experts using the criteria and scoring system defined in the Evaluation Criteria.
 Applicants will be notified of the evaluation results within four weeks after completion of the panel ranking.
 Each applicant will receive an Evaluation Summary Report (ESR) containing individual scores, comments, and the final consensus assessment.
 The successful applicant will be invited to sign a Financial Support Agreement with 28DIGITAL on behalf of the LLM-BRIDGE Consortium.
 Evaluation criteria: 
 The evaluation is based on the following criteria, each with a maximum score and a minimum threshold:
 Relevance (maximum score: 10; threshold: 6): Assessment of how well the proposal aligns with the objectives of LLM-BRIDGE, including its capacity to support early-stage Generative AI startups and contribute to European GenAI strategic goals.
 Track record (maximum score: 8; threshold: 5): Evaluation of the applicant’s proven experience in incubating and scaling AI or deep-tech ventures, with demonstrated results in terms of startup growth and innovation.
 Networks and access (maximum score: 8; threshold: 5): Consideration of the ability to provide startups with access to mentors, investors, and strategic industry partners that can strengthen their market positioning and growth potential.
 Adaptability (maximum score: 6; threshold: 4): Evidence of flexibility and capacity to respond to emerging technological and market needs, particularly in the rapidly evolving Generative AI sector.
 Monitoring framework (maximum score: 5; threshold: 3): Quality and clarity of the proposed processes and documentation for monitoring and reporting, including well-defined metrics to track startup progress and overall programme performance.
 Cost effectiveness (maximum score: 5; threshold: 3): Adequacy and justification of the proposed budget, demonstrating efficient use of resources and value for money.
 Each criterion is scored from 0 up to its maximum (10, 8, 6 or 5). Proposals are evaluated according to six qualitative levels.
 Not addressed (score 0 in all scales): The proposal fails to address the criterion or cannot be assessed.
 Poor (score 1–2 out of 10, 1–2 out of 8, or 1 out of 5/6): The proposal shows serious weaknesses or lacks the required level of detail.
 Fair (score 3–4 out of 10, 3–4 out of 8, or 2 out of 5/6): Some strengths are present, but significant weaknesses remain.
 Good – threshold level (score 5–6 out of 10, 5 out of 8, or 3–4 out of 5/6): The criterion is adequately addressed, though moderate weaknesses are observed.
 Very good (score 7–8 out of 10, 6–7 out of 8, or 4–5 out of 5/6): The criterion is well addressed, with only minor shortcomings.
 Excellent (score 9–10 out of 10, 8 out of 8, or 5–6 out of 5/6): The criterion is fully addressed, demonstrating outstanding quality with no or only negligible weaknesses.
 Threshold per criterion: 3 to 6 points. Overall minimum score: 26 points (out of 42). Maximum total score: 42 points. Proposals failing to reach the threshold in any criterion or the overall minimum score will not be considered for funding.
description: The Venture Incubation Programme (VIP) serves as an instrument to strengthening incubation capacity in Europe to support early-stage GenAI ventures as well as to:
 Accelerate the commercialisation of LLM technologies, providing mentoring, access to high-performance computing (HPC) resources, data infrastructures, and regulatory guidance.
 Promote responsible AI innovation, aligned with the AI Act, Data Act, GDPR, and the EU’s Digital Decade Targets.
 Foster cross-border collaboration, knowledge sharing, and participation of underrepresented regions and groups in the European AI ecosystem.
 Through this call, LLM-BRIDGE seeks to identify and support one high-quality, EU-based incubator capable of supporting startups in the transforming of early-stage GenAI ideas into viable, scalable, and ethically compliant ventures that may be eligible to apply for the future Long Jump and European Grand Challenges. Participating in the VIP provides an opportunity for a leading incubator to position itself at the forefront of Europe’s generative AI revolution. This collaboration offers strategic, reputational, and operational advantages, aligning the incubator with a pan-European initiative that seeks to redefine the future of AI-driven innovation and technological leadership. 
 The VIP programme will select one incubator to run a 12-week VIP cohort across Europe, which will:
 Deliver structured training and mentoring to 30 startups.
 Provide and facilitate access to technical expertise and AI infrastructures.
 Monitor and report progress using standardised KPIs defined in the Annex I. 
 Contribute to the overall impact of LLM-BRIDGE and the European GenAI innovation ecosystem.
 The selected incubator will gain direct access to a carefully selected pipeline of high-potential GenAI startups from across Europe, allowing it to deepen its expertise in nurturing deep-tech ventures with the potential to drive the next wave of generative AI solutions. Such engagement not only enhances the incubators reputation as a leading enabler of cutting-edge innovation but also strengthens its market position within the highly competitive AI ecosystem.

beneficiaryAdministration: Applications follow a two-stage process . Stage 1 applications must be submitted through the EIT Culture & Creativity online submission platform by 30 October 2026, 17:00 CET . Following admissibility and eligibility checks, eligible Stage 1 proposals are independently evaluated by two external experts against Excellence, Impact, Quality and efficiency of implementation, and EU dimension. Proposals must meet all individual thresholds and achieve at least 23/30 points . Up to 30 selected applicants will be invited to Stage 2 and receive a EUR 20,000 fixed lump sum to prepare a Business Development Plan.
 Stage 2 is open only to applicants selected following Stage 1. Full proposals must be submitted by 15 March 2027, 17:00 CET and are evaluated by four independent external experts: two technical/thematic and two business/financial experts . Proposals must achieve all applicable thresholds and at least 70/90 points to proceed to the internal portfolio selection, which includes a hearing and carries up to 40 additional points. Projects must obtain at least 24/40 points in portfolio selection. Final ranking is based on the combined external quality evaluation and portfolio selection scores, subject to available budget.
description: The Innovation Projects call supports high-impact, close-to-market innovations at TRL 7 , enabling their progression towards TRL 9 and full market deployment in the Architecture, Audio-Visual Media and Fashion sectors. EIT Culture & Creativity financial support may cover up to 70% of the eligible project costs used to establish the project-based lump sum .

titulo: European Network of Factcheckers
texto:
es_SortDate: 2026-08-10T00:00:00.000+0000
beneficiaryAdministration: The Emergency Response Support Grants are designed to enable fact-checkers to respond rapidly and effectively to disinformation during crisis events across Europe as well as to build crisis capacity through preparation activities. This grants are the part of FACTEUR: Fact-Checkers for European Resilience Against Disinformation project implemented by
 The European Fact-Checking Standards Network (EFCSN) with seven partner organisations – Pagella Politica/ Facta, Faktograf, Newtral, Fact Review, Greece Fact Check, Fact Check Cyprus and Science Feedback.
 Background 
 Information crises are characterized by the emergence of an "information vacuum”, a critical window where the demand for reliable news far outpaces the supply of verified facts. It is within this vacuum of high uncertainty that disinformation thrives, often overwhelming the regular response capacities of media and fact-checking organizations.
 We define an information crisis as the disruption of the information system characterized by a surge in the volume and intensity of disinformation within public and digital spaces.
 This involves the deliberate spread of false or misleading content intended to deceive the public, cause harm, or achieve political, economic, or security gains, and triggering further social and political escalations in information space including hate speech, inciting public panic, increased societal polarization and institutional mistrust, threats to collective safety, and both online and physical attacks against specific social groups.
 An information crisis is often, but not always, determined by a crisis event. We divide these crisis events into three main categories: predictable, semi-predictable and unpredictable. For more information, refer to the Crisis Events Taxonomy .
 While unpredictable information crises leave little room for maneuver, predictable events allow organizations to utilize the available lead time to pre-emptively build resilience and prepare their response strategies.
 FACTEUR project established a standardized taxonomy of crisis events, allowing teams to assess their technical, human, and financial readiness and to formulate strategic plans for foreseeable crises.
 Acknowledging that while not every crisis event will inevitably escalate into a full-scale information crisis, it is highly recommended to monitor the information ecosystem closely and prepare for potential escalation whenever such events occur. 
 Furthermore, the FACTEUR project recognises that an information crisis may emerge in one country without necessarily manifesting in another, as the potential for a situation to escalate into a full-scale information crisis often depends on specific national contexts and societal resilience. However, national-level crises are frequently exploited by disinformation actors to establish or reinforce specific disinformation-based narratives that then become cross-European. In this context, coordinated Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI) operations, as long-lasting structured activities with dedicated infrastructure, can act as a powerful amplifier, strategically weaponizing crisis events, to boost their impact and scale narratives across borders. At the same time, FIMI operations possess the capacity to generate crises at both national and international levels. 
 Activities 
 Fact-checking organisations can request support for the following grants:
 1. Emergency Fact-Checking Grants are aimed at:
 Crisis fact-checking, debunking and investigative reporting which includes hiring additional journalists and fact-checkers,
 Advancing technical capabilities to monitor and react to disinformation which includes procurement and upgrading AI and other monitoring and verification tools,
 Publishing counter-narratives and analysis of information crisis which can include production costs, translation, and other, 
 Enhancing crisis communication, engagement and reach of fact-checking activities which can include creation of multimedia content and cooperation with other media and content creators,
 Other activities related to specific crisis event needs which are clearly demonstrated in application.
 2. Emergency Capacity-Building Grants are aimed at: 
 Improve organizational security and legal protection in the scope of preparation activities for crisis events,
 Enhance crisis preparedness and development of organisational protocols, trainings and mentorship, 
 Improve technical capabilities to monitor disinformation campaigns and FIMI operations, 
 Analyse disinformation ecosystem that can be activated in the crisis events,
 Strengthen cross-border cooperation in order to enhance responses to crisis events that are common for certain region or cultural and political context,
 Strengthen the capacity to detect and debunk AI-generated content during crisis. 
 Eligibility Criteria 
 To be eligible for funding, applicants must meet the following requirements:
 Legal entity: Applicants must be a legal entity, whether for-profit or non-profit.
 Certification: Applicants must be EFCSN certified fact-checking organisations or fact-checking organisations that can demonstrate that they respect in practice the European Code of Standards for Independent Fact-Checking Organisations, including but not limited to transparency of funding, staff and governance.
 Fact-checking: Applicants must be fact-checking organisations or fact-checking teams or units within larger organisations. Fact-checking is defined as the use of an evidence-based method to verify the accuracy of claims made in the public sphere. Applicants must publish at least four human-authored, original fact-checking articles a month on average. 
 Location: Organisations must be based in the European Union or DEP-associated countries (please consult this document for the most updated version).
 Single applicants or consortia: This call is intended for both single applicants, and consortia of organisations. All members of the consortium must comply with all eligibility criteria. Any organization can receive funding for Emergency Capacity-Building Grants only once during the call duration. Any organization can receive funding twice for Emergency Fact-Checking Grants during the call duration. An exception may be made for unpredictable crises events affecting multiple countries, allowing an eligible organization to receive a third grant. 
 Budget, Funding, Payment Terms, Grant Duration 
 Total Budget for Emergency Response Support : 450.000€ (225.000€ for Emergency Fact-Checking Grants and 225.000€ for Emergency Capacity-Building Grants)
 Maximum Project Amount: €30.000. Exact amount must be calculated using this template table.
 Funding Rate : 50%
 Maximum Grant Amount: 15.000€
 Form of Grant: lump sums
 Eligible costs: 
 Direct costs: Salaries and compensations, volunteer costs (in line with daily rates listed here), consultants, mentors, equipment, online/IT tools, travel and accommodation, translation, legal costs, production costs (graphic design, multimedia content creation, etc) and other costs related to activities.
 Indirect / Administrative Costs: Indirect costs cover organisational overhead directly related to managing this support request (e.g. staff time spent coordinating, administration). These are capped at 10% of total direct costs.
 Number of Grants: ~30 (15 for Emergency Fact-Checking Grants and 15 for Emergency Capacity-Building Grants)
 Payment Structure: 50% upon approval of request, 50% following the approval of the final report.
 Retroactive costs: If a grant is approved, costs that are presented in the budget are eligible from the time of application submission.
 Max. Grant Duration: 8 months
 Selection Procedure 
 The evaluation will be conducted in three phases:
 Phase 1: Eligibility & Compliance: The EFCSN team will perform an initial check to ensure all applications are complete, meet the basic requirements and applicants are eligible.
 Phase 2: Expert Evaluation: Requests will be evaluated by the consortium experts based on need, urgency, regional vulnerability, and the applicant’s capacity to absorb the support. EFCSN will oversee the process, ensuring transparency, financial safeguards, and equitable distribution. Applications will be assessed against the award criteria outlined below.
 Category
 Description
 Max. points
 Need
 Clear evidence of crisis event occurring during or after the project and organisational needs related to unpredictable crisis events.
 10
 Urgency
 Time-sensitive circumstances where absence of support would meaningfully worsen the outcome.
 10
 Regional Vulnerability
 Context of operating environment — political, economic, or press freedom constraints that amplify organizational risks in case of crisis events.
 10
 Absorptive Capacity
 Organisational ability to receive, manage, and account for the funds in a timely manner.
 10
 Phase 3: Approval: All grant applications that received at least 30 points will be reviewed and approved by the WP4 Consortium Decision Body. 
 How to Apply and Timeline 
 This call is open from 10 August 2026 on a rolling basis but no later than 31 December 2027 or until funds are depleted. 
 To apply, please fill out this application form on the EFCSN Grants Platform. Note that you will need to register an account if you have not already.
 Please note that all budgeted costs should reflect the market rates. Requests will be evaluated within 3 working days for unpredictable crises and 30 working days for predictable and semi-predictable crises. 
 Rejected applicants may appeal within 5 working days . The Governance Body delegates the final review, which must be resolved within 15 working days.
 Reporting 
 An outcome report is expected from all grant recipients no later than 30 days after completion of the project (max. 8 months).
 Transparency Notice 
 This call has also been published on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal. Funding granted through this call will be disclosed on: https://efcsn.com/funding-opportunities . Disclosure will cover the name of the receiving organisation, amount, and grant duration.
 NB! If a grant recipient operates in a high-risk environment or handles sensitive data, they may request that their identity remains confidential during the implementation phase and be disclosed after the end of the funding cycle.
 Questions? 
 Please send questions about this call to grants@efcsn.com .

 Background 
 Information crises are characterized by the emergence of an "information vacuum”, a critical window where the demand for reliable news far outpaces the supply of verified facts. It is within this vacuum of high uncertainty that disinformation thrives, often overwhelming the regular response capacities of media and fact-checking organizations.
 We define an information crisis as the disruption of the information system characterized by a surge in the volume and intensity of disinformation within public and digital spaces. 
 This involves the deliberate spread of false or misleading content intended to deceive the public, cause harm, or achieve political, economic, or security gains, and triggering further social and political escalations in information space including hate speech, inciting public panic, increased societal polarization and institutional mistrust, threats to collective safety, and both online and physical attacks against specific social groups. 
 An information crisis is often, even if not always, determined by a crisis event. We divide these crisis events into three main categories: predictable, semi-predictable and unpredictable. For more information, refer to the Crisis Events Taxonomy .
 The FACTEUR project recognises that an information crisis may emerge in one country without necessarily manifesting in another, as the potential for a situation to escalate into a full-scale information crisis often depends on specific national contexts and societal resilience. However, national-level crises are frequently exploited by disinformation actors to establish or reinforce specific disinformation-based narratives that then become cross-European. In this context, coordinated Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI) operations, as long-lasting structured activities with dedicated infrastructure, can act as a powerful amplifier, strategically weaponizing crisis events, to boost their impact and scale narratives across borders.
 Activities 
 Fact-checking organisations can request support for the following activities:
 Production of Fact-sheets – brief overviews in English of the most prevalent disinformation narratives and claims surging during ongoing semi-predictable and unpredictable crises events that may have cross border impact. Fact-sheets are intended to inform fellow fact-checkers, catalyse knowledge sharing and warn the community of potential spill-over effects in ongoing crisis situations;
 Production of Case studies – post-crisis analysis in which fact-checking organizations document disinformation surges during semi-predictable and unpredictable crisis events and their actions and experiences in order to share the know-how throughout the community. 
 Crisis events that are subjects of the Fact-sheets and Case studies must happen during the duration of the call . Both outputs need to be delivered in English and according to templates provided as Appendix 1 (Fact-sheets) and Appendix 2 (Case studies). Both outputs will be shared with the fact-checking organisations via the designated platform.
 Eligibility Criteria 
 To be eligible for funding, applicants must meet the following requirements:
 Legal entity: Applicants must be a legal entity, whether for-profit or non-profit.
 Certification: Applicants must be EFCSN certified fact-checking organisations.
 Fact-checking: Applicants must be fact-checking organisations or fact-checking teams or units within larger organisations. Fact-checking is defined as the use of an evidence-based method to verify the accuracy of claims made in the public sphere. Applicants must publish at least four human-authored fact-checking articles a month on average.
 Location: Organisations must be based in the European Union or DEP-associated countries (please consult this document for the most updated version).
 Single applicants: This call is intended for single applicants. Organizations can receive funding for production of fact-sheets and case studies multiple times.
 Budget, Funding, Payment Terms, Grant Duration 
 Total Budget for Emergency Response Support: 50.000€
 Maximum Project Amount: 2.000€ for fact-sheets and 7.000€ for case studies. Exact amount must be calculated using the template table.
 Funding Rate: 50%
 Maximum Grant Amount: 1.000€ for fact-sheets and 3.500€ for case studies.
 Form of Grant: lump sums
 Eligible costs: 
 Direct costs: Salaries and compensations for translation, other costs related to activities.
 Indirect / Administrative Costs: Indirect costs cover organisational overhead directly related to managing this support request (e.g. staff time spent coordinating, administration). These are capped at 10% of total direct costs.
 Number of Grants : ~20
 Payment Structure: 100% following the delivery of outputs.
 Retroactive costs: If a grant is approved, costs are eligible from the time of application submission.
 Max. Grant Duration: 1 month for fact-sheets and 3 months for case studies.
 Selection Procedure 
 The evaluation will be conducted in three phases:
 Phase 1: Eligibility & Compliance: The EFCSN team will perform an initial check to ensure all applications are complete, meet the basic requirements and applicants are eligible.
 Phase 2: Expert Evaluation : Requests will be evaluated by the consortium experts based on need, and the applicant’s capacity to absorb the support. EFCSN will oversee the process, ensuring transparency, financial safeguards, and equitable distribution. Applications will be assessed against the award criteria outlined below.
 Category
 Description
 Max. points
 Need
 Clear evidence of ongoing/finished semi-predictable or unpredictable crisis event and its influence on European Information system
 10
 Absorptive Capacity
 Organisational ability to receive, manage, and account for the funds in a timely manner.
 10
 Phase 3: Approval: All grant applications that receive at least 14 points will be reviewed and approved by the WP4 Consortium. 
 How to Apply and Timeline 
 This call is open from 10 August 2026 on a rolling basis, but no later than 30 April 2028 or until funds are depleted. 
 To apply, please fill out this application form on the EFCSN Grants Platform. Note that you will need to register an account if you have not already.
 Requests will be evaluated within 3 working days for factsheets, and 7 working days for case-studies from the application submission. 
 Rejected applicants may appeal within 5 working days. The Governance Body delegates the final review, which must be resolved within 15 working days.
 Reporting 
 Grantees are obliged to submit the final output (fact sheet/case study) to the EFCSN grant OR community platform . Upon confirming that the outputs are in compliance with the grant requirements, EFCSN will issue an email notice of successful completion. All outputs will be published on the EFCSN grant OR community platform . 
 Transparency Notice 
 This call has also been published on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal. Funding granted through this call will be disclosed on: https://efcsn.com/funding-opportunities/ . Disclosure will cover the name of the receiving organisation, amount, and grant duration.
 NB! If a grant recipient operates in a high-risk environment or handles sensitive data, they may request that their identity remains confidential during the implementation phase and be disclosed after the end of the funding cycle.
 Questions? 
 Please send questions about this call to grants@efcsn.com .
